• Sound creative judgment and the ability to give specific, constructive feedback that improves the work.

• Clear written, verbal, and visual communication skills, including experience presenting and building alignment with cross-functional partners.

• Comfort balancing creative ambition with audience needs, business goals, timelines, budgets, and production constraints.

• The ability to move between strategic thinking and hands-on creative development in a collaborative, fast-moving environment.

• Experience creating culturally resonant work that earned organic conversation, press, or community participation.

Duolingo has over 500 million users and is rapidly expanding across new subjects and markets, meaning our growth trajectory is central to our business success. We're hiring a Senior Data Scientist to execute and improve our foundational monetization (revenue) forecast, used for planning, goal setting, and business strategy.

This person will be part of our Monetization Data Science team, collaborating with peers and cross-functional partners in Finance, Product, and Strategy to continuously improve our forecasting capabilities. They will drive methodological advances and deliver trustworthy business-critical quarterly forecasts in close partnership with the Finance team. Built on a deep understanding of the dynamics of revenue generation across Duolingo’s product portfolio, the forecast will set the pace for monetization innovation and inform business operation and strategy.

• Co-own forecast development and presentation with Finance team peers. Recommend, develop and validate methodological advances to our forecasts, aligning methodological strengths with business priorities.

• Work with diverse stakeholders to develop forecasts that reflect a deep understanding of our product development, big bets, and evolving business strategy.

• Translate complex analytical findings into clear narratives for senior leadership and cross-functional partners. Influence strategic decisions through a combination of technical depth and effective communication.

• Build systems and processes that ensure our forecasting process is robust, repeatable, and easily understandable across the company.

✅ You have...

• Applied industry experience building forecasts in messy real world settings where details, confounds, and the validity of assumptions matter.

• A graduate degree in Data Science, Statistics, Economics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent demonstrated expertise in formal analytical techniques.

• Demonstrated ability to connect technical results to real-world recommendations, and to translate product and business changes into technical requirements.

• Strong command of SQL, Python, AI analysis tools, and data/analytics engineering ecosystems.

• Exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to distill complex quantitative work into crisp, actionable insights for diverse audiences.

⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...

• Experience operating in a financial analytics role at a high-growth consumer technology, finance/banking, or consulting company, including experience with revenue forecasting specifically.

• Experience at a public company, including the analytical demands that come with investor-grade reporting and forecasting.

• An impressive Duolingo streak.

As a Staff Security Engineer, you will shape and deliver Duolingo’s security strategy, safeguarding our learners, employees, systems, and services. You’ll identify the highest-impact security problems, lead complex initiatives from proposal through production, and build durable security capabilities across our applications and cloud infrastructure. Working across Engineering, Product, Legal, Finance, and IT, you’ll make practical risk decisions, establish secure-by-default patterns, and help teams ship safely at scale. This role is based in New York City. We know great candidates bring different combinations of experience. If you meet some or most of the qualifications below, we encourage you to apply!

:brain: You will...

• Set technical direction for security across Duolingo’s applications, cloud infrastructure, and engineering systems.

• Lead complex, multi-team security initiatives from problem definition and design through implementation, measurement, and ongoing ownership.

• Design and build scalable security services, controls, and automation that prevent, detect, and remediate risks with minimal manual effort.

• Partner with engineering teams to threat model systems, review architecture and code, prioritize risks, and deliver practical mitigations.

• Strengthen security across the software-development lifecycle, including secrets management, dependency security, vulnerability management, and CI/CD controls.

• Evaluate Duolingo’s security posture, use evidence to identify the highest-impact investments, and define measurable outcomes for security programs.

• Lead technical response to significant security incidents and translate lessons learned into lasting improvements.

Hinge is the dating app designed to be deleted

In today's digital world, finding genuine relationships is tougher than ever. At Hinge, we’re on a mission to inspire intimate connection to create a less lonely world. We’re obsessed with understanding our users’ behaviors to help them find love, and our success is defined by one simple metric– setting up great dates. With millions of users across the globe, we’ve become the most trusted way to find a relationship, for all.

About the Role
Hinge is the dating app designed to be deleted, and our mission is to inspire intimate connection to create a less lonely world. Hinge Futures is a small, product-focused team that gathers evidence and builds conviction around which long-term investments are worth pursuing (and which should not be pursued). Futures forms hypotheses based on shifts in Gen Z culture, emerging technology, and changing ideas about trust and safety, and then builds narratives, prototypes, and environments for daters to experience first-hand and respond to.

When an idea earns conviction, it hands off to Product and Tech. When it doesn't, we share the learning and refine our hypotheses and continue experimentation.

We're looking for a Design Lead with experience in speculative futures and concepting. You're comfortable experimenting with emerging tech, you can turn an idea into a concrete prototype or experience, and you like figuring out what's possible before anyone else does. You'll work closely with our creative technologist and researcher to build things Gen Z daters can try, so we can learn what's worth betting on.

What You'll Do
•
Design to test, not to ship. Turn a strategic hypothesis into a concept, then into a prototype (an interface, an object, an environment, a ritual) fast enough to learn from it.

•
Collaborate with partners. Brief, critique, and elevate external studios and freelance talent, and know when it's faster to make it ourselves.

•
Tell the story. Build the narratives and artifacts that make a speculative concept legible to leadership, product teams, and participants.

•
Work in the open. Show rough work early, invite critique, and make it easy for others to react to something real.

•
Bridge to Product. Partner with Product, Design, and Engineering so the ideas that survive are ready to scale, and the ones that don't are documented well enough to teach us something.

•
Treat AI as a material. Explore generative tools and AI-native interaction with taste and a critical eye, including where they should not be used.

Who You Are
•
You have 5-7+ years of experience in product, interaction, experience, or industrial design, with a portfolio that shows range from speculative work to shipped product.

•
You have a strong, defensible point of view on craft, and you can explain why a choice is right for a person, not just for a metric.

•
You move from idea to rough prototype quickly, using whatever gets you there: Figma, motion, code, physical mockups, AI-assisted tools.

•
You've worked in a lab, studio, agency, or R&D setting, or have an equivalent record of making new things where no playbook existed.

•
You're at ease without a brief. You can write the brief, and kill your own idea when the evidence says to.

•
You're curious about Gen Z culture, dating, intimacy, and trust, and about how people really feel about the technology in their lives.

How We Work
•
Prototype over pitch. We'd rather show a rough thing than a polished deck.

•
Evidence over opinion. Every world we build exists to test a hypothesis, and we follow what we learn.

•
Provocation with a point. Weird is welcome when it teaches us something.

•
Short sprints, small team. Few people, fast loops, and a lot of trust.

•
Hand it off well. Our work succeeds when Product and Tech can pick it up, or put it down, with confidence.

As a member of our team, you’ll enjoy:

401(k) Matching: We match 100% of the first 10% of pre-tax 401(k) contributions you make, up to a maximum of $10,000 per year.

Professional Growth: Get an annual Learning & Development stipend once you’ve been with us for three months. You also get free access to Udemy, an online learning and teaching marketplace with over 6000 courses, starting your first day.

Parental Leave & Planning: When you become a new parent, you’re eligible for 100% paid parental leave (20 paid weeks for both birth and non-birth parents.)

Fertility Support: You’ll get easy access to fertility care through Carrot, from basic treatments to fertility preservation. We also provide a stipend towards fertility preservation. You and your spouse/domestic partner are both eligible.

Date Stipend: All Hinge employees receive a $100 monthly stipend for epic dates– Romantic or otherwise. Hinge Premium is also free for employees and their loved ones.

ERGs: We have eight Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)—Asian, Unapologetic, Disability, LGBTQIA+, Raices, Women/Nonbinary, Parents —that hold regular meetings, host events, and provide dedicated support to the organization & its community.

At Hinge, our core values are…

Authenticity: We share, never hide, our words, actions and intentions.

Courage: We embrace lofty goals and tough challenges.

Empathy: We deeply consider the perspective of others.

We're continuing to invest heavily in building the best creator platform with the best team in the creator economy and are looking for a Porto Site Lead to support our mission.

This role is based in Porto, Portugal and operates on a hybrid work model (in-office 3 days per week).

About the team

Trust & Safety keeps Patreon welcoming and fair, so creators and their fans can connect and creativity can thrive. We set clear standards and act quickly and consistently when something's off.

Porto is our main Trust & Safety hub in Europe, where a significant share of our safety work gets done. It's a close-knit, multidisciplinary team of content specialists, project and program managers, vendor managers and policy experts, sharing the office with colleagues in Support, Fraud and Compliance. As Patreon grows into a place where fans discover new creators and communities, the work done in Porto matters more than ever.

About the role

We're looking for an experienced operations leader to run Trust & Safety in European hours and lead our Porto site.

As T&S Operations Lead, you'll own how well Porto runs: healthy queues, targets met, smooth handoffs to our US team, and a team that knows what's expected and how they're doing. Operational excellence, team enablement, and capacity planning are at the heart of the job.

You'll be the senior operations leader on site from day one, with a direct report focused on operations enablement and a scope built to grow as Porto does, including leading more of the site's team over time. You'll work hand in hand with our global Trust & Safety leaders on policy, quality, tooling, and partner management, and bring Porto's perspective into the decisions that shape how we keep Patreon safe.

As Porto’s Site Lead, you’ll represent the whole office, not just T&S. You'll serve as Porto’s site representative: chairing the Porto Leadership Council, partnering with Workplace/HR, and bringing the needs of Compliance, Fraud, Support Experience, and T&S into site-wide decisions.

What you'll do

• Run European-hours operations to target. Co-own queue health, review rates and service levels with the leaders of each safety area while Porto is online. Spot drift early, fix what you can, and escalate the rest with a clear owner and timeline.

• Plan capacity. Work with the leaders of each safety area and our program managers to build monthly capacity plans across our in-house team, outsourcing partners and automation, and rebalance work when volume shifts.

• Deliver on our targets, and find out why we miss. The leaders of each safety area set targets for their work and agree them with you. You'll be the single place those goals come together for Porto: deliver them on the ground, track progress, coach the team, and dig into root causes when we miss on efficiency or quality, then bring back what you learn.

• Raise the bar on how we operate. Co-own the playbooks, training and workflow changes our safety-area leaders and program managers design, lead their rollout in Porto, and measure the impact on quality, handle time and backlog.

• Keep work moving between Europe and the US. Make sure escalations, incidents and open work hand off cleanly across time zones, so nothing stalls or drops.

• Lead incidents in European hours. Contain issues using our playbooks, make the call when a decision can't wait, and hand off with full context.

• Look after the team. Make sure people doing high-exposure work have the rotation, breaks and support they need, notice early signs of strain, and involve people before changes that affect them.

• Lead the site. Chair the Porto Leadership Council, bringing together every team in the Porto office, from Support to Fraud and Compliance. Be Porto's voice with US leadership, and build a culture where people feel connected and recognized.

• Grow Porto's team and leaders. Develop your direct report and the site's emerging leaders, and help Porto keep a strong mix of specialist, project, program, and policy talent.

What you'll own

• Your call, for Trust & Safety in Porto: running our operations day-to-day in European hours. That includes keeping work flowing when volume spikes, covering absences, containing incidents using our playbooks, and setting the team's operating rhythm. Other teams in the office keep their own leadership.

• Your call, for the Porto site: the Porto Leadership Council’s agenda and how Porto shows up with Execs and US leadership. Other non-T&S teams keep their own leadership. You align and represent them, you don’t manage them.

• Agreed with the leaders of our safety areas: the targets they set for their work, monthly capacity plans, shifting work between areas, and workflow changes that affect enforcement decisions.

• Owned by partners, with your input: policy and enforcement standards, quality standards, HR matters and vendor contracts. You'll have a strong voice in all of them.

About you

• 8+ years leading content moderation, Trust & Safety or customer support operations. Whether in-house or at an outsourcing partner, you've run the people, targets, and quality of a content or customer-facing team. Workforce management and quality leadership in those settings count too.

• You have a track record of moving the numbers. You've owned throughput, quality, and service-level goals for an operations team, built capacity plans, and delivered measurable improvements you personally drove.

• You've scaled operations with outsourcing partners or automation.

• You lead with clarity and fairness. You set expectations, give direct feedback with care, and stay calm when things get hard.

• You work well across teams. You've led alongside teams you don't manage, and you know when to decide and when to align.

• You're fluent in English. Portuguese is a strong plus.

• You're based in Porto, or ready to relocate. We'll support your move.

Nice to have

• Trust & safety experience, especially with EU/UK online-safety rules.

• Experience leading a site or office in Portugal or elsewhere in Europe.

• Experience with AI-assisted moderation or quality programs.

What success looks like in your first year

• Review rates and handoffs in European hours are consistently on target.

• T&S has a clear, reviewed capacity plan, updated monthly.

• Quality findings turn into action within 90 days.

• The Porto Leadership Council meets on a regular cadence with agreed site priorities.

• The Porto team feels more connected and more confident in where they're headed.

Why join

• Lead a site. Shape how our main Trust & Safety hub in Europe runs, with real decision rights from day one.

• Room to grow. A clear path to leading more of Porto's team as the site grows.

• Meaningful work. Help keep a community of millions of creators and fans safe.

• Life in Porto. One of Europe's most livable cities, on the Atlantic coast.

How to apply

Along with your CV, answer one short question (a few sentences is plenty): tell us about an operation you led. How many people, what volume, and one metric you improved? If one of our recruiters reached out to you, we'll cover this in your first call instead.

We hire talented and passionate people from different backgrounds because workplace diversity and inclusion is critical to our ability to serve creators worldwide. If you’re excited about a role but your past experience doesn’t match with every bullet point outlined above, we strongly encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re a creator at heart, are energized by our mission, and share our company values, we’d love to hear from you.

Patreon powers creators to do what they love and get paid by the people who love what they do. Our team is passionate about making this mission and our core values come to life every day in our work. Through this work, our Patronauts:

• Put Creators First | They’re the reason we’re here. When creators win, we win.

• Build with Craft | We sign our name to every deliverable, just like the creators we serve.

• Make it Happen | We don’t quit. We learn and deliver.

• Win Together | We grow as individuals. We win as a team.

The New York Times' Accounting team is looking for a Senior Accounting Analyst who has knowledge reviewing contracts and transactions. You will determine proper accounting treatment, and record following generally accepted accounting principles. You can query and analyze data sets, summarize data in a concise and meaningful manner, and highlight insights that help inform validating recorded transactions. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Senior Accounting Manager. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

About the Role

As a Senior Accounting Analyst, you will participate in month end closing work including the preparation of journal entries and balance sheet account reconciliations. Have the opportunity to recommend, document, and implement processes to facilitate the proper accounting of revenue and expense contracts. Furthermore, you will collaborate with partners to foster communication, learn about new contracts and products, improve processes, and to ensure the accuracy of accounting and reporting.

Responsibilities:

• Review customer contracts and other transactions and ensure/document the proper accounting following ASC 606 or other relevant accounting standards.

• Build case-specific appeal strategies supported by clinical records, research, payer policies, coding guidance, and applicable appeal requirements.

About the role:

Every risk control at Branch, whether for fraud, financial crime, disputes or collections, answers two questions. The first is detection: should this user, login or transaction be flagged? The second is treatment: once it is flagged, what happens to the user, how quickly, and how does a legitimate user get back to normal? Our rules team owns the first question. This role owns the second.

As Risk Controls Manager, you own the control paths users move through once a control fires: step-up verification, holds, locks, review queues, unlock and recovery, and the handoff to offboarding. You decide who goes down each path, when, and on what exit criteria, across onboarding, login and account takeover, money movement and card activity, for fraud, financial crime, disputes and collections alike, including how Branch treats scams and first-party fraud. You also build and run Branch's User Risk Score, the user-level view that decides which treatment each user gets. Then you make the changes happen.

The role exists to close the gap between a strategy decision and the frontline. You will take ideas from the Enablement Director and carry them through Product, Engineering, Operations and our BPO partner until they are live, measured and understood by the people working the queues.

This is an individual contributor role with program ownership. You will not have direct reports.

Responsibilities:

Own the Control Paths and User Risk Score

• Map and document every control path Branch uses today: the trigger, the treatment, the owner, the service level and the exit criteria for each

• Set the standard for which treatment applies to which risk, so similar risks get similar treatment across products and channels

• Keep the map current as rules, products and vendors change, and make it the reference Operations, Support and Product work from

• Document each control path, with its rationale, approvals and change history, to a standard our partner banks, internal audit and examiners can follow, and support partner bank reviews, audits and exams of the control environment, working with Compliance

• Build and run Branch's User Risk Score: a lifetime view of each user that starts at enrollment and moves with behavior, money movement, payouts and account changes. You own the factors, weights, risk bands and the treatment each band receives; the Enablement Director owns the score's results and approves material changes

• Combine existing signals (device and login intelligence, transaction monitoring, disbursement and payout models, organization risk classification, dispute and collections outcomes) into a single user-level view, working with the Manager of Risk Rules and Monitoring and Data

• Measure and tune the score on capture rate, false positive rate and approval-rate cost, and feed confirmed fraud back into it, so every user removed changes how the next one is scored

• Set the identity verification and step-up standards for phone and chat contacts, including unlocks and ATO recovery, and close the social engineering gaps the Manager of Risk and Recovery Contact Operations surfaces from live contacts

Change Management & Operationalization

• Use loss, friction and operational data to find the paths that cost the most in loss, user friction or manual work, and redesign them

• Write the requirements for each change, sequence it with Product and Engineering, and run it from design through testing to live

• Before a change goes live, map its upstream and downstream impacts on disputes, collections, Support and other control paths, so a fix in one place does not create loss, friction or volume in another

• Measure each change after launch and report whether it did what it was meant to do

• For every control change, update the operational side before it goes live: queue design, SOPs, BPO procedures and agent guidance, working with the Managers of Risk and Recovery Program Operations and the BPO partner

• Write procedures that meet audit and partner bank requirements and that an agent can still follow in the middle of a live queue

• Brief Operations on what changed and why, so the frontline understands the controls it works with

• Consult on improvements that start inside Operations; those remain with the Managers of Risk and Recovery Program Operations

Protect Good Users

• Own the friction legitimate users absorb from fraud controls: step-up pass and drop-off rates, time to unlock or resolve, and the volume of escalations controls create

• Design recovery paths for account takeover victims and good users caught by a control, in partnership with Support

• Track loss on users released from controls, so friction reductions are not paid for in fraud

Scams and First-Party Fraud

• Design the treatment paths for scams: warnings and added friction on high-risk outbound payments (P2P, Branch Direct, instant transfer), protective holds when a user appears to be acting under a scammer's direction, and recovery paths for scam victims, in partnership with Support

• Build first-party fraud factors into the User Risk Score, such as repeat or unsupported disputes, bust-out patterns, negative-balance abuse and payback failures. Set the treatment each band receives, from limits to dispute scrutiny to offboarding

• Apply Branch's scam and first-party fraud definitions consistently across control paths. Set the standard, with Disputes Operations and Compliance, for separating authorized scam payments from unauthorized transfers at the handoff to disputes

Onboarding Guardrails

• Bring Risk & Recovery's control requirements to the cross-functional onboarding review led by the User Onboarding Product Manager, who owns the onboarding experience end to end

• Model the risk and conversion tradeoff of proposed step-up and verification changes; Product makes the final call, and agreed tradeoffs are documented

• Able to size exposure and measure friction, false positives and loss from data; SQL and BI fluency

The Role

The best software companies don’t grow through direct sales alone. They grow through ecosystems: networks of partners who extend their reach, deepen customer relationships and deliver outcomes no single company can deliver alone. Technology partners sit closest to the product. They are the platforms, data tools and AI services our customers already use, and how well Braze works with them shapes what customers can build.

Technology partnerships at Braze take three forms. Product partnerships are built into the product, where Braze and a partner’s technology work together for customers. Strategic partnerships are held at a senior level with a small number of platform companies, including the major cloud and large language model providers. And a long tail of ISVs integrate with Braze and extend what customers can do. Each form has grown on its own terms, and the strategy that connects them is still being written.

This role is key to that strategy. Reporting to the AVP, Partner Experience, you own the strategy, program and plan for technology partnerships in all three forms, and you define it in close collaboration with the VP, Technology Partnerships, who leads the strategic relationships. That means deciding what a technology partner is at Braze, what each type gets from us and what we expect back, and how product, strategic and ISV partnerships fit together, so that partners, Product and the field see one ecosystem rather than three separate efforts. This role owns the strategic and program layer that turns that strategy into something partners and internal teams can actually run on.

You will work closely with Product, the Competitive and Monetization Strategy team, Partner Operations and Business Systems, and alongside the Partner Programs Director, whose tiering, benefits, incentives, portal and directory your program runs within. Several parts of the technology program are ready to be rebuilt, including ISV onboarding and evaluation, co-sell and how competitive situations are handled. We need someone who has built a technology partner program before, to decide what stays, what changes and what goes, and to set a plan for the next 24 months.

Salesforce has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Braze. The agreement has not yet closed and remains subject to customary closing conditions. If it completes, there will be work over the next few years to bring the Braze partner program in line with the broader Salesforce partner program and ecosystem, and this role will play an important part in that.

What You’ll Own

• Technology partnerships strategy, program and plan. Own the strategy, program and plan for technology partnerships across product, strategic and ISV partners, including partners that have a commercial motion with Braze and partners that do not. Define the strategy in close collaboration with the VP, Technology Partnerships, so it reflects the strategic relationships they lead as well as the ISVs beyond them, and agree the plan with them before it goes wider. Set out what good looks like, in what order, and who needs to do what.

• What a technology partner is. Draw the line between an ISV partner, which has an integration with Braze, and a technology partner, which has a commercial motion with Braze. The two overlap, but not every ISV has a commercial motion: some bring value through the product alone and help customers reach specific use cases. Define what each gets from Braze and what Braze expects in return, within the tiering, benefits and incentives set by the Partner Programs Director.

• Product partnerships. Bring product partnerships, ISV partnerships and technology partnerships into alignment with Product. Product partnerships are led category by category, so map what exists, agree with the category leads what counts as a partnership, and make sure technology partners have access to, and awareness of, the Product Roadmap.

• The ISV program. Following the defined ISV strategy, rebuild the ISV program: how new ISV partners are evaluated, how they are onboarded, and an ideal partner profile (IPP) that tells the team where to invest. Make onboarding something a partner can complete without chasing, and measure how long it takes for a partner to become active.

• Co-sell and referrals. Own and scale the co-sell program for technology partners. Take an early trial and turn it into a repeatable program, then run it with other partners: how partners are chosen, how opportunities are shared, how it connects with Sales and what we measure. Design a referral program that works in both directions between Braze and technology partners.

• Competitive rules of engagement. Work with the Competitive and Monetization Strategy team to define when a technology partner becomes a competitor and the rules of engagement in those situations. Optimise and scale a universally adopted, ongoing competitive process for technology partners, so that every partnership decision follows the same logic.

• Directory listings outside marketplace. Own Braze listings in other companies’ directories, such as AI-platform directories like Gemini. A customer cannot buy Braze through these listings, which separates them from marketplace work. Work with the Lead Partner Program Manager (Channel & Marketplace) to keep that line clear: if Braze can be bought through it, it belongs to marketplace, and if it is only a listing, it belongs here.

• Evaluating the program. Evaluate the technology partner program and refine the strategy for the next 24 months. Work out where technology partners create value, whether through pipeline from a small number of partners or product adoption across the long tail, and where they do not. Recommend what to keep, stop and start.

• Reporting. Work with Partner Operations and Business Systems to replace separate reports with single views of what is working, such as partner-influenced pipeline, co-sell opportunities, time to activate and customer adoption of integrations.

• Cross-functional alignment. Work with Product, Partner Marketing, Partner PMM, Partner Operations and Business Systems so the program’s rules, tools and messages agree with each other, and bring what you hear from technology partners into the tiering, benefits and incentives that the Partner Programs Director owns.

• Salesforce alignment. If the acquisition completes, lead the work to bring the technology partner program in line with the broader Salesforce partner program and ecosystem.

What This Role Is Really About

Strong partner-influenced pipeline, a co-sell program that repeats, ISVs that onboard quickly and customers who adopt integrations are signs that technology partnerships are working. The strategy sits behind them.

The real work is deciding what technology partnerships are for at Braze, and making sure every form pulls in the same direction. A strategic partnership with a cloud or AI platform, a product partnership built with a category lead and an ISV with a single integration all affect the same customers. When they are planned separately, partners hear different things from different teams and the field cannot tell which partner to bring into a deal. When they share a strategy, a program and a plan, Braze can choose where to invest, say no with a reason and show the value.

You will not manage a team. You will not own the strategic relationships, Product’s roadmap or the competitive strategy, and you will not control the priorities of the people closest to them. The strategy is set together with the VP, Technology Partnerships: they bring the strategic relationships and you bring the program that connects them. Your impact comes from being clear, being right and being someone that Product, the VP, Technology Partnerships and the Partner Experience team want to work with. The best version of this role is a strategist who has built technology partner programs at a larger company, knows which parts of that playbook fit a company our size, and leaves out the rest.

How We Show Up

• Charts strategy across every form. You work with the VP, Technology Partnerships to decide what good looks like for technology partnerships when product, strategic and ISV partnerships have each grown on their own, and you build the model rather than wait for someone else to define it.

• Influences without authority. You don’t own the strategic relationships, Product’s priorities or the competitive strategy, but you shape all three through the quality of your thinking and the trust you build.

• Connects the dots. You see how a partner’s integration, commercial motion, directory listing and place in the Product Roadmap fit together, and you say so clearly.

• Decides with evidence. You work out where technology partners create value and where they don’t, and you stop what isn’t earning its place.

• Right-sizes the program. You know what a mature technology partner program looks like at a larger company. You choose what Braze needs now and show the path to the rest.

The Role

As Director, Partner Strategy & Programs, you’ll set the direction for how Braze builds, invests in and grows its partner ecosystem. You’ll decide where we compete through partners, which partners and motions earn investment, and how the program structure turns that strategy into partner behavior and business results.

You’ll be a senior advisor to Partnerships leadership and a connector across the partner organization. You’ll set the framework that our Partner Program Managers, Partner Development, Partner Sales, Partner Marketing and Operations teams work within. The tiered Alloys program is one of the most important levers you’ll own. It’s a means to the strategy, not the whole job.

What You’ll Lead

• Ecosystem strategy. Define the multi-year strategy for the Braze partner ecosystem: where partners create the most value for customers and for Braze, how the mix of Technology, Marketplace and Delivery partners should change, and which partner motions deserve investment. Turn that into a clear, prioritized roadmap that leadership can fund and the organization can carry out.

• Program architecture. Own the design of the Alloys Partner Network: tiering, benefits, incentives and requirements. Make sure it rewards the partner behaviors that drive customer outcomes and revenue. Start with a candid assessment of what works today, and lead the program’s evolution through a phased plan that fits our scale.

• Partner economics and investment. Build the business case behind how we invest in partners: margins, referral fees, rebates, market development funds and benefits. Bring clear recommendations to the SVP, Partnerships, tie every investment to a measurable return, and reallocate spend away from what doesn’t perform.

• Ecosystem integration and scale. Prepare the program for its next stage, including fitting with the broader Salesforce partner ecosystem if the acquisition completes. Find where the two programs complement each other, where they conflict, and how to move partners across with minimal disruption.

Set the strategic requirements for the systems partners interact with, including the MindMatrix partner portal (launching in January), the Partner Directory and the Alloys brand identity. Business Systems, Brand and Partner Marketing own the build. You define what success looks like and hold it to that standard.

• Capability standards. With Partner Education, define the certification and enablement standards that make tier status a reliable signal of partner capability and customer readiness.

In your first year, Braze has a clearly stated ecosystem strategy that leadership has bought into. The Alloys program is redesigned around the behaviors that matter most. What This Role Is Really About

A department our size can't hire a specialist for every function, and shouldn't. What it needs is someone who can pick up whatever matters most this month, run it properly and leave something behind that works without them. One month that is the narrative and run of show for Forge Partner Day. The next it is an initiative that three teams each assume another team owns. The through-line is visibility: whatever you are working on, people can see where it stands.

You will not own the content or the decisions. Pillar leads own their numbers and their stories, and leadership owns the choices. You own the delivery and the clarity around it. That means asking the question that exposes a gap in a plan, noticing when a deadline will slip a week before it does, and telling a leader that their narrative buries the lead. You do this without formal authority, and you earn trust by making everyone else's job easier.

You will also see things that are sensitive: survey results, plans in progress, changes to the organisation. Discretion is part of the job.

How We Show Up

• Drives ownership to completion. You step in to claim unassigned initiatives, assign clear accountability, and steer them through to successful execution.

• Communicates with clarity and impact. You distill complex updates into concise, actionable briefs for leadership and facilitate decisive, productive meetings.

• Ensures end-to-end transparency. You maintain clear and dependable tracking of progress, status, and risks, flagging delays early alongside practical solutions.

• Leads through influence and trust. You motivate senior leaders to hit deadlines by making collaboration seamless and consistently delivering value.

• Balances strategy with tactical detail. You seamlessly transition from managing detailed operational schedules to briefing executives on complex cross-functional dependencies.

• Upholds strict confidentiality. You handle sensitive and unreleased information with complete discretion and earn executive trust.

Who You Are

• 5-8 years in program management, project management or strategy and operations roles at a B2B SaaS or technology company, ideally supporting a go-to-market, partnerships or alliances team

• Has driven cross-functional programs from brief to delivery with several stakeholders and senior people, and has run events or company moments with speakers, content and a tight timeline

• Has built visibility across a portfolio of workstreams, using trackers, status reporting and tools such as Jira, and knows how to keep them honest without making them a burden

• A strong writer and storyteller, able to turn updates and numbers into something leaders grasp quickly

• Skilled at facilitation: you run meetings with senior people, keep them to time, and leave with clear actions and owners

• Data-driven, comfortable building trackers and spotting when numbers don't add up

• Highly organised, able to manage many deadlines and very different kinds of work at once without losing detail

• Happy to build process from nothing, and pragmatic about keeping it light enough to survive a busy quarter

• Comfortable with the tools that run a department, such as Google Workspace, Slack, Jira and Confluence

Braze is also starting to deliver more certified metrics through semantic models and AI agents in Snowflake. • Own metric definitions end to end. Get the teams involved to agree on one canonical definition, document it, and state plainly what each model measures and where it stops

• Shape how the team builds. Help set and evolve our development, testing, and code review standards. Review pull requests, mentor teammates, and consolidate models that past projects left redundant

• Cut through ambiguity in both directions. Help stakeholders turn loose questions into precise asks. Help our data teams align on what a request means, which model it belongs in, and who should build it. Communicate clearly enough that everyone ends with the same understanding

• dbt and SQL in Snowflake: expert SQL and modular, DRY dbt development, including dimensional modeling, snapshots and incremental models, tests beyond uniqueness and not-null, and thorough documentation. You understand Snowflake performance and cost trade-offs

• Model and metric design: you design for grain, history, and reuse so the next project doesn't need a rewrite. You can walk us through shipped data products and the trade-offs behind their design

• Requirements from ambiguity: you turn loosely defined asks and undocumented processes into precise definitions and requirements

• Cross-team collaboration: you've worked through models and systems you didn't own and got changes made by building agreement across teams

• Technical leadership: you mentor others, review code carefully, and set standards teammates follow

• AI that makes your team better: you've shipped reusable workflows, skills, or tools that teammates adopted and that measurably improved how the team works. You use your experience to speed up the people around you as well as your own work

• Domain knowledge: GTM operations, post-sale, or business operations data in SaaS, such as CRM opportunities and accounts, marketing lifecycle, professional services, and customer success platforms

• Independent delivery: you scope, sequence, and communicate your own projects, including status and trade-offs

• You've built semantic models or certified metric definitions used by AI or conversational analytics (for example Snowflake Cortex Analyst or the dbt Semantic Layer), including test question sets to evaluate answers

• You've worked with data observability or data catalog tools

Why This Role, Why Now

Braze is the leading customer engagement platform, helping the world's most ambitious brands build absolutely engaging relationships with their customers. Our services are how those brands get from signed contract to real value: Onboarding gets them live, Success ensures they can scale, Deliverability protects their reputation from the first send, Training builds the skills to use Braze well, and Support keeps them running at scale.

This role owns how that services portfolio goes to market. You'll be the product marketer for every post-sales offering: Training, Support, Success, and our professional services, including Onboarding, Deliverability, Technical Account Management, and more. Your job is to make these offerings easy to understand, easy to buy, and easy for the field to sell, so more customers get the expertise that makes them successful on Braze.

This is a role for a builder who understands that selling expertise is different from selling software. You'll work shoulder to shoulder with our Services, Support, and Education leaders, plus Sales, Customer Success, Pricing, and your Product Marketing peers, to turn a set of offerings into a coherent portfolio with a clear story.

What You'll Own

• Services portfolio positioning and messaging. One clear narrative for Training, Support, Success, and professional services that ladders up to the core Braze platform story and the customer outcomes we promise.

• Packaging and pricing input. Partner with Services leadership, Pricing, Finance, and Deal Desk to shape the services catalog: what we offer, how it's bundled and tiered, and how it shows up on an order form. Simplify where the catalog has grown complicated.

• Services attach strategy. Define where services belong in the customer lifecycle (new business, onboarding, expansion, renewal, product launches) and build the plays that increase attach rate at each moment.

• Field and Customer Success enablement. Make sure Sales, Services Consulting, Customer Success, and Account Management can position services with confidence and connect them to customer outcomes.

• Voice of the customer for services. Bring customer, field, and market insight back to the Services org to inform which offerings we build, retire, or reshape.

What You'll Do

• Make the intangible tangible. Turn services into clear value propositions with defined outcomes, use cases, and proof, so a buyer understands what they get and why it's worth paying for.

• Build the services messaging architecture. Create the framework, offering descriptions, and proof points that every team uses, from the website to the order form to the renewal conversation.

• Shape the catalog with Services and Pricing. Bring market and competitive insight to packaging decisions, rationalize overlapping offerings, and make sure what we sell is easy to buy and easy to deliver.

• Launch new and updated offerings end to end. Take services launches from positioning through packaging, pricing communication, enablement, and field readiness.

• Build attach plays that get run. Identify the triggers for each offering (a new logo, a migration, a new channel, a product launch, a renewal) and build the plays, talk tracks, and assets that help the field act on them.

• Create assets the field actually uses. Pitch decks, one-pagers, service descriptions, proposal language, value stories, web pages, and customer stories.

• Connect services to product launches. Partner with your Product Marketing peers so new Braze capabilities launch with the right Training, Onboarding, and Support story attached.

• Reach existing customers. Partner with Customer Marketing, Lifecycle, and Web to build awareness of services across the installed base.

• Measure what matters. Track attach rate, services bookings, and enablement adoption, and report results to Services, Sales, and Marketing leadership.

Who You Are

• Fluent in services. You understand how services are scoped, sold, priced, and delivered, and you know that selling expertise is different from selling software.

• A packaging thinker. You see a catalog as a product. You can tell when an offering is confusing, overlapping, or hard to buy, and you know how to fix it.

• A storyteller. You make outcomes concrete. Buyers and the field understand what a service does for them, not just what it includes.

• Field-obsessed. You build for the rep, the CSM, and the services consultant in the deal. If an asset doesn't get used, it doesn't count.

• A collaborator. You're a sleeves-rolled-up, low-ego operator who earns trust with the Services org and gets things shipped without direct authority.

• Data-driven. You instrument your work and connect it to attach and bookings with real numbers.

How Success Is Measured

Success is measured against business outcomes, not activity: services attach rate on new and renewal deals, services bookings, and field adoption of services plays and assets.

In your first year, success means:

• A services messaging framework and simplified catalog that Sales, CS, and Services all use.

• Packaging and pricing improvements shipped in partnership with Services, Pricing, and Finance.

• Attach plays running in the core sales and renewal motions, with measurable lift in attach.

• Trusted relationships with Services, Support, Success and Education leaders. You're the person they pull in early.

What You'll Bring

• 7+ years of experience in services marketing (preferred) or product marketing at a B2B technology company.

• Hands-on experience marketing post-sales offerings such as professional services, support tiers, training and certification, or customer success programs.

• Strong PMM fundamentals: messaging frameworks, positioning, value propositions, and launch execution.

• Experience with packaging and pricing, ideally for services or add-on offerings.

• A track record of building sales and CS enablement (pitch decks, playbooks, talk tracks, one-pagers) that gets adopted in the field.

• Experience driving measurable attach, upsell, or expansion through marketing programs.

• A proven ability to work cross-functionally and execute without direct authority in a fast-moving, matrixed organization.

• Excellent written and verbal communication, comfortable presenting to executives, the field, and customers.

Nice to Have

• Experience working inside a Services, Support, Education, or Customer Success organization.

• Experience in martech, customer engagement, or adjacent SaaS categories.

• Familiarity with email deliverability, IP warming, or messaging infrastructure.

• Experience with partner-delivered services or a services partner ecosystem.

Our Mission and Opportunity

Early education is one of the most important determinants of childhood outcomes, a critical support for working families, and a $175B market that remains underserved by modern technology. Brightwheel is the largest, fastest growing, and most loved platform in early ed, trusted by millions of educators and families every day. We are a three-time Cloud 100 company , backed by top investors including Addition, Bessemer, Emerson Collective, Lowercase Capital, Notable Capital, and Mark Cuban.

Our Team

Our team is passionate, talented, and customer-focused. We embody our Leadership Principles in our work and culture. We are a distributed team with remote employees across every US time zone, as well as select offices in the US and internationally.

Who You Are

You are an AI-native product leader and builder who combines world-class product taste, deep customer empathy, and high standards with the drive to build something new, and you want that something to matter. You create clarity in ambiguous spaces, turn a first product line into a real business, and lead by example in how modern products get built. You care about the teacher who opens the app at 7:25 with nine toddlers arriving, the parent who wants to know their child is learning, and the state official who has to show what a year of funding bought. You move with the urgency and ownership of a founder.

You will succeed in this role if you are

• Here for the mission. You want the outcome measured in what children learn and what teachers can do, and you know that a business that grows is how that outcome reaches millions of children instead of thousands.

• Focused on customer and business impact. You care about creating real value for families and educators, and about proving a business that can grow into something meaningful for brightwheel.

• A practitioner-builder. You do not lead from a distance. You use AI and modern tooling in your own work to build, prototype, and learn, and to show what great looks like.

What You'll Do

The years before kindergarten shape everything that comes after, and early education is where the gap between children first opens. brightwheel sits at the center of it, trusted by tens of thousands of schools and millions of families, with the distribution and profitable core most founders never get to start with. Our education business is where that trust turns into outcomes: curriculum that gives a teacher a plan for the day, assessments that show a parent how their child is growing, and professional development that helps teachers get better at one of the hardest and least supported jobs in education. States and districts fund these years, set the standards, and need to see results against them. Entire companies exist to do just one of these pieces. None of them also runs the school.

The opportunity now is to make education brightwheel's second core business, ten times its current size, and to put a real curriculum, a real measure of growth, and real training in front of children, teachers and families who have never had them: new segments, from states and districts to the smallest programs; new models, from digital subscriptions to multi-year contracts; and products that improve what children learn, on top of running the programs that teach them.

You will lead that work. You will take education from early traction to product-market fit in segment after segment, building with your own hands and with AI, and proving both the product and the business behind it. The mission reaches more children only if the business grows.

In this role, you will

• Own the education business end to end, from product-market fit in new segments into scale.

• Discover what teachers, directors, parents and district buyers truly need, build the first version, and get it in front of real people quickly.

• Prove the business behind each bet: the value to customers, the model, and the economics that make it worth growing.

• Build hands-on, using AI and modern tooling to prototype, learn, and raise what a small, focused team can accomplish.

• Work directly with our CEO and executive team, set the vision and drive outcomes visible at the Board level.

• Recruit, inspire, and grow the team around the bets that take off.

What You've Done

We are open to a variety of backgrounds, but qualified candidates usually bring:

• A record of building products customers love. You have the product taste and judgment to know what to build and what to leave out, and the customer empathy to find real needs before the data exists.

• Experience taking something from 0 to 1 or 1 to 10. You have started or built something new, ideally to real traction, and ideally as a founder or early builder who wore every hat.

• Ownership of the whole business. You have carried the value, pricing, and economics that turn an idea into something worth scaling.

• Applied AI in your own work. You use AI and modern tooling to build and ship faster, and to go deeper across disciplines.

• Communication and presence. You can set a vision, align an executive team and board, and inspire the builders who join you.

What Sets You Apart

The candidates who will thrive in this role go beyond strong product management:

• You are a multidisciplinary builder. You move across product, design, engineering, and data, and you use AI to go deeper in each.

• You thrive in ambiguity. You make confident calls when there is no playbook and no data, and you follow the data the moment it exists.

• You think like an owner of the whole business, from the customer problem to the path to revenue, and you bring an executive team and a board along with a clear, compelling vision.

Our Team

Our team is passionate, talented, and customer-focused. We embody our Leadership Principles in our work and culture. We are a distributed team with remote employees across every US time zone, as well as select offices in the US and internationally.

About the role

At brightwheel, we are moving to a way of working where a person decides what should be built and why, directs AI agents to do the work, and owns the result, while the agents work around the clock. This applies across engineering, product, design, and the rest of the company.

A large part of Platform Engineering's work is building the foundation that makes this possible: the platform that our people and their agents work on, and the safeguards that let agent work reach customers without lowering quality or trust. We measure the result in how much each person can deliver and how quickly it reaches teachers and families.

Most of the design decisions are still open. As a Principal AI Platform Engineer, you will set the direction for distinct areas of that foundation, own them for the long term, and run them as internal products. You will build them and answer for whether people use what you build, whether it stays reliable, and what it changes for them.

Design gets argued out between the people closest to the problem, and a named person owns every change. Your peers are senior engineers from backend, infrastructure, web, and mobile, and they will argue with your designs as you will with theirs. The role is remote.

Who You Are

You solve hard problems by building systems that other people depend on. You may have built an agent or developer platform before. You may instead come from distributed systems, infrastructure, developer tools, or product engineering. Either way, you have built agents or agent infrastructure that a team relied on, you direct agents in your own work, and you want to apply what you have learned to brightwheel's own problems, starting from how our teams work today. You will do well here if you:

• Set technical direction on your own initiative. You start from a business problem, work out the technical problem behind it, and bring a recommendation for how to solve it.

• Watch how people do the job today, then earn adoption with software that works.

• Argue design with your peers, in writing and in person, and change your mind when the evidence calls for it.

• Move fast without giving up quality or reliability. You decide with the information you have, ship, and adjust from what you learn.

• Make what you build observable, so that anyone who depends on it can tell what it is doing and catch a problem early.

What you’ll do

• Decide the direction for your areas, and settle the shared decisions with the other senior engineers leading this work.

• Keep quality, security, and reliability high as the volume of agent work grows. In your areas, decide what agents are allowed to access, make what they do traceable, and decide where a person needs to stay involved.

• Extend what works beyond engineering, so product, design, and teams in every part of the company can rebuild how they do their work.

• Identify what limits how much work people can hand to agents, and build the infrastructure that removes those limits.

• Shorten the time from an idea to a change customers can use, by removing the manual steps and waits in between.

• Adopt tools that already work instead of rewriting them, and turn them into shared standards.

• Teach engineers across the company to direct agents and check their output, so teams can do this without waiting on you.

What you’ve done

Qualified candidates usually bring:

• A complex system or platform they designed and built that many people or teams came to depend on, with evidence of its adoption and results.

• Agents or agent infrastructure they built that a team relied on, with the checks, access limits, and logging that made it safe to trust.

• A record of directing agents to increase their own output and impact, and of teaching teams to do the same.

• Slow or manual work they removed for other people, with before and after numbers.

• Technical direction they wrote that other teams then built from.

• Engineers they mentored who now own harder problems.

What sets you apart

• You have built agent infrastructure used across several teams, and you can show how much of their work ran through it.

• You have run agents unattended on real work, and you know what it takes to trust the result.

• You have taken this way of working beyond engineering, to product, design, or another function.

• Data: PostgreSQL and Redis

• Frontend: React with TypeScript

• Mobile: native iOS with Swift, Android with Kotlin

• Cloud and infrastructure: AWS and Kubernetes

About CareMessage

CareMessage is a social enterprise and the largest patient engagement platform for low-income populations in the United States. We deliver personalized health education and care coordination through text messaging — reaching patients where they already are, in the language they speak, at the moments that matter most. Unlike technology built for large health systems and adapted down, CareMessage is designed from the ground up for organizations serving low-income, historically marginalized communities.

Why Join Us in Leveraging Technology to Improve Health Equity

Many of us have had the experience of doing good work or building great products, but wondering if it is truly making an impact. At CareMessage, our mission is clear: improve health equity for low-income populations across the United States. Every role here connects directly to that purpose. We care deeply about the communities we serve, and we also hold a high standard for performance, collaboration, and integrity.

Our ideal team members:

• Deliver meaningful, measurable results

• Invest in their teammates and build trust

• Seek feedback and continually grow

• Stay steady and solutions-oriented in ambiguity

• Lead with integrity and responsibility

• Communicate with clarity and empathy

If you are motivated by impact, energized by collaboration, and ready to do some of the most meaningful work of your career, we encourage you to apply. If this sounds like you, we would love to meet you.

_____________________________________

About the Role

This is a builder’s job in the Office of the CEO. You will turn CareMessage’s strategy into the philanthropic capital that funds it, carry the funder relationships and the impact story that keep that capital renewing, and work AI-first so that one senior person can run a program that would normally take a team. You will need to learn how we operate and what we do well enough to speak and write about it accurately on your own, because the purpose of this role is to take that work off our executive team’s plates.

CareMessage is building the first social impact engine for the 90 million low-income people the health system was never designed to serve, and philanthropy determines how fast we get there. On a forward-looking, run-rate basis, our Core subscription business nearly covers the operating costs of service delivery, so philanthropy funds what we build next and subsidizes the safety-net organizations that cannot yet pay in full. Our Board has activated a 2026 to 2029 Growth Case calling for roughly $40 million in philanthropic investment, about half of it confirmed. We already have more funder relationships and opportunities than we can pursue well, so much of the job is helping us be selective in line with our organizational goals. The CEO and executive team remain the relationship owners and champions for our most significant funders; you run everything underneath those relationships, and full ownership, including of relationships that are smaller today, will be handed to you as trust is established. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports.

What You Will Do

A. Know our work and connect our strategy to the capital that funds it.

• Learn our organizational strategy, the key initiatives underway across CareMessage and the sources of truth behind them, along with our platform, our customers and our evidence, well enough to speak and write about them accurately on your own, so that what you produce comes to the executive team for a review and never for a rewrite.

• Working with the CEO and executive team, translate each strategic priority into the funders, asks and structures that can fund it, prioritizing unrestricted, multi-year funding wherever we can, and keep that map current as the strategy evolves.

• Run the institutional pipeline: qualify the opportunities already in front of us against our organizational goals, identify new foundations, corporate funders and, selectively, public funders, bring two to three major new partners a year into active cultivation and say no, respectfully, to the rest, with every stage, owner, next step and renewal date kept current in one system of record.

• Execute our place-based philanthropy playbook, proven in Texas where a foundation partnership alongside the state’s primary care association turned a single grant into a regional ecosystem and a larger multi-year commitment, in the next regions where we prioritize regional ecosystems in line with our Growth Case priorities, working with local and national funders.

B. Design, write and deliver the grants and the reports.

• Design each ask with its executive sponsor so it sits at the intersection of the funder’s strategy and ours: what we are asking for, how it is structured (restricted or unrestricted, single year or multi-year) and what we will be able to report.

• Write letters of inquiry, concept notes, proposals, budgets and narratives that are precise, evidence-based and in our voice, built from verified product, outcomes and financial data, and tailored to how each funder actually makes decisions.

• Own reporting on every active commitment: the calendar, the compliance requirements, and reports that say exactly what we can and cannot yet claim, including the difference between patients reached and outcomes improved.

• Collaborate with colleagues across the organization, including Finance, Product Development, Data, Clinical, Customer Experience, Growth, and Compliance and Risk, to bring the right information, evidence and alignment into every proposal, report and funder conversation.

C. Tell the impact story and carry our external relations.

• Produce the annual impact report and the funder-facing updates between reports, drawing on our evidence base (peer-reviewed studies and the outcomes data we generate) and our customer stories to present our impact accurately and compellingly.

• Own donor communications across institutional funders, Board giving and the individual pipeline: the materials Board members use to open doors, acknowledgments, and the cadence of touchpoints between asks.

• Run the cadence of funder conversations, read the signals in them, and decide when to act yourself and when to bring in the CEO and/or executive sponsor; carry the relationships handed to you as trust is established.

• Represent CareMessage with the associations, networks, peer organizations and ecosystem partners whose relationships lead to funders, and explain our platform, our data infrastructure and our use of AI to program officers and partners in plain language.

D. Build the AI-first engine behind all of it.

• Design, document and run the AI-enabled workflows the function relies on, for prospect research, drafting, reporting and meeting preparation, with verification steps, data rules and disclosure norms aligned with our AI governance and with each funder’s own policies.

This role is designed for high-potential university graduates who possess a "Business-Critical Mindset" and the ability to understand how technical solutions can impact customer operations and improve efficiency, resulting in platform adoption and long-term ROI for our customers.

• Support Strategic Implementations: Support the implementation of Celonis Platform as a business-critical tool by connecting customer data to actionable strategic outcomes.

• AI-Forward Solutioning: Leverage your technical background to build and deploy "AI-forward" solutions, utilizing Machine Learning and LLM integrations for our most strategic customers.

• Stakeholder Engagement: Actively participate in discovery and requirement workshops, practicing a consulting mindset to communicate technical findings to business stakeholders and continue building the solution with a strong customer centric mindset.

• Business Analytics, Academy and Global Programs

• Business Apps & Product and Engineering

• Solution Architecture & Celonis Support

• Academic Background: A recent graduate (or final year student) with a degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Business Information Systems, or a related technical field.

• Business-Critical Mindset: A strong interest in how technology creates financial value. You are driven by outcomes like ROI, efficiency, and process improvement.

You’ll own a meaningful slice of the product: the important-but-less-nebulous work that keeps a democracy-facing platform trustworthy and scalable. You’ll also own the internal tools that let our program managers run local campaigns at scale, and the testing and analysis that tells us whether what we shipped actually worked.

You’ll join the team building a new platform that bridges divides to regularly identify what constituents truly agree on and help turn it into effective policy and action. They understand and embrace AI as a means to multiply their output and replace toil with leverage. Most critically they want to be part of a pragmatic and ambitious team made up of the best people in the world operating with integrity and urgency. At the same time, AI-driven economic and social disruption will demand faster, more effective government responses than our institutions are built to deliver. We are building a product to surface the public will on major issues by combining large-scale civic input with informed, representative dialogue, then activate that will at scale by mobilizing millions to shift the incentives that shape public policy. By using the same technologies that threaten democratic legitimacy, we aim to give citizens more voice than ever before, identify shared agreement across political differences, and enable collective intelligence at scale.

Change.org is a public benefit company and the world’s largest social change platform, with 100M users and more than 40,000 campaigns launched monthly. This team will operate as a start-up within Change.org , benefiting from strong culture, stability and mission orientation.

• Own the product work that keeps a democracy-facing platform trustworthy: moderation systems and rubrics, privacy and policy obligations (such as GDPR), and the due diligence that comes with a product close to public officials and public decisions.

Much of what they do to scale campaigns, like city research, decision-making, and building materials for local government partners, isn’t productized yet. You’ll partner with a dedicated engineer to change that, treating ops as a core customer.

• Be the key liaison to the program managers who run our deliberation cycles. Support and coordinate across campaigns from the product side, from platform setup and audience acquisition through in-cycle monitoring and post-cycle reporting, so we build a cohesive product with them in mind and carry their insights, and those of our decision-maker users, back into what we build.

• Own experimentation and analysis: design and run A/B tests, carry testing through after features launch so it doesn’t pile up, instrument cycles, build dashboards, and write up findings the team can act on. • Manage external partners and vendors—paid acquisition partners, tooling vendors, contractors, and other external collaborators—so internal partners aren’t task-switching into vendor coordination.

• Connect the pieces across groups, particularly marcoms and program management, so campaigns, launches, and product changes stay coordinated. Take the “par-baked” first pass on analyses and synthesis so product, design, and engineering can move faster.

• Handle user inbound requests, monitoring and creating a system to respond and learn from these inputs

• Extend the product management and design functions where needed—running discovery, drafting briefs, herding cross-functional initiatives, and bringing things over the line in code with the help of our Claude-centered AI development process.

You treat internal tools and operational workflows as a product surface—designing, instrumenting, and iterating on them the same way you would on a feature. You’re comfortable owning the unsexy middle, and you get satisfaction when something boring becomes automatic.

• AI Fluency: You use AI tools fluently to multiply your output—drafting, analyzing, coding, automating, evaluating. You can stand up an LLM-based eval, run a deep research pass, or wire up a small agentic workflow to replace a manual task. You understand the difference between what AI is good at and where a human still needs to sit in the loop.

You’re comfortable in spreadsheets, SQL, and product analytics tools, and you know how to combine quantitative signal with qualitative read to tee up decisions. About Us

With electric vehicles expected to be nearly 30% of new vehicle sales by 2025 and more than 50% by 2040, electric mobility is becoming a reality. ChargePoint (NYSE: CHPT) is at the center of this revolution, powering one of the world’s leading EV charging networks and a comprehensive set of hardware, software and mobile solutions for every charging need across North America and Europe. We bring together drivers, businesses, automakers, policymakers, utilities and other stakeholders to make e-mobility a global reality.

Since our founding in 2007, ChargePoint has focused solely on making the transition to electric easy for businesses, fleets and drivers. ChargePoint offers a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to create an all-electric future and a trillion-dollar market.

At ChargePoint, we foster a positive and productive work environment by committing to live our values of Be Courageous, Charge Together, Love our Customers, Operate with Openness, and Relentlessly Pursue Awesome. These values guide how we show up every day, align, and work together to build a brighter future for all of us.

Join the team that is building the EV charging industry and make your mark on how people and goods will get everywhere they need to go, in any context, for generations to come.

Reports To

Vice President, Global Channel Sales

What You Will Be Doing

At ChargePoint, we are building the fueling network of the future, and our channel partners are critical to our strategic expansion. As the Senior Director of NAM Channel Sales, you will be the strategic leader responsible for architecting and executing our entire North American reseller and distribution strategy. You will empower and scale a high-performing channel sales organization to drive market penetration, accelerate revenue growth, and dominate the EV charging landscape. This is a senior leadership role where your strategic vision, commercial acumen, and ability to build a world-class partner ecosystem will directly impact our regional revenue goals and global sustainability mission.

In this strategic leadership position, you will manage, scale, and mentor a team of channel sales professionals responsible for driving revenue through our reseller partners. Your day-to-day will involve shaping the strategic direction for partner recruitment, enablement, and performance management. You will partner closely with executive sales leadership and cross-functional teams to close high-stakes, partner-led enterprise deals. You will act as a key advisor to both our most strategic partners and our internal product and marketing teams, translating market and partner feedback into actionable strategies that shape our future growth. Success in your first 6 to 12 months means establishing a highly scalable channel sales playbook, optimizing the partner lifecycle from onboarding to sales execution, and delivering significant, measurable growth in channel-driven revenue.

What You Will Bring to ChargePoint

• Lead and Scale the Channel Organization: Hire, train, and mentor a high-performing team of Partner Account Managers, guiding them through complex sales cycles, partner development, and enterprise-grade opportunity scoping.

• Architect the Channel Strategy: Own the technical and sales enablement strategy for our partner ecosystem. Ensure our reseller partners are equipped with the solutions, training, and tools required to effectively sell ChargePoint’s hardware, software, and services.

• Drive Partner Performance: Set clear performance objectives and sales targets for the NAM reseller channel. Monitor and analyze channel sales performance, implementing strategies to optimize results and exceed revenue goals.

• Foster Executive Relationships: Cultivate and maintain strong, lasting relationships with the executive leadership at our most strategic reseller partners, acting as a dedicated executive sponsor to drive mutual growth.

• Optimize Channel Operations: Establish and refine scalable channel sales playbooks, partner onboarding frameworks, and standardized documentation to shorten sales cycles and dramatically improve win rates.

• Align Cross-Functional Strategy: Partner directly with the SVP of Sales and collaborate with Marketing, Product Management, and Solutions Engineering to align channel strategies with overarching regional revenue goals and market expansion targets. Product Management, and Solutions Engineering to align channel strategies

• Champion Market Insights: Serve as the leading voice for the channel within ChargePoint. Gather and share partner feedback and market insights to drive product improvements and enhance the overall partner experience.

• Navigate Deal Complexity: Act as a senior escalation point for critical, partner-led enterprise opportunities, directly assisting in negotiating and resolving complex commercial and deployment challenges.

Requirements

• 12 - 15 years of channel management or channel sales experience, with a proven track record of supporting complex enterprise sales cycles through a partner-led model.

• 5 - 8 years of direct people-management experience at the Director level or equivalent, with demonstrated success in scaling a team.

• Deep familiarity with the EV charging industry, renewable energy, or a related technical field.

• Bachelor's degree in Business, Sales, Marketing, or a related field (MBA preferred).

• Demonstrated ability to develop and execute a comprehensive channel sales strategy that drives significant revenue growth.

• Exceptional capability to translate complex technical and commercial details to both executive and partner audiences.

• Results-oriented mindset with a track record of meeting and exceeding sales targets in a channel environment.

• Proficiency in CRM systems, sales tracking tools, and the Microsoft Office suite.

Location

Vancouver, BC - Remote

The proven ability to translate technical financial data into clear, informative reports

Advanced Excel skills

French fluency

Internal or external auditing expertise
