DonorsChoose is an education nonprofit ensuring every US public school student has the classroom resources they need to learn, grow, and thrive.

Founded by a teacher in 2000, DonorsChoose connects educators with a nationwide community of supporters who believe investing in students today will transform tomorrow. Educators request the materials they know their students need, and donors can choose the classroom, community, or cause they want to support. Since our founding, donors have supported 90% of US public schools. Every request is vetted, resources are delivered to classrooms, and donors can see the impact of their support through transparent reporting and updates from students and teachers. Raising $1.9 billion for classrooms, DonorsChoose has earned top ratings from Charity Navigator, GuideStar, and CharityWatch for its transparency, trust, and impact. Our dedicated team works from across the United States to turn resources into opportunities for students and teachers.

About the Content Operations Team

The Content Operations team has a front-row seat to the most compelling classroom-generated content on our site. We review all incoming project requests, and help deliver the final touch to funded projects to donors: the donor thank-you “package.” When donors give to a project on our site, they receive direct follow-up from the classroom, including a letter, photos of the project in-action, and handwritten student thank-yous .

Our goal is to guide, approve, and leverage this content to deliver a personal experience that inspires donor and partner loyalty.

About the Role

The Volunteer Coordinator is responsible for supporting key aspects of our NYC-based Gratitude volunteer program.

Donors who give above a certain threshold can opt in to receive physical thank-you notes from students, which are physically mailed to our NYC offices for review by our team of local in-person volunteers.

That’s when the Volunteer Coordinator and their team and your team (including dozens of in-person Gratitude volunteers ) comes in! The Volunteer Coordinator plays a pivotal role in ensuring that our volunteers feel supported, and that student thank yous are successfully and speedily reviewed so that eager donors can receive their notes as quickly as possible!

Responsibilities

• Represent gratitude operations by fostering an inclusive and productive in-person volunteer environment. (75%)

• Prepare for daily programming such as organizing volunteer stations and workspaces.

• Support daily volunteer operations. This could mean: scheduling, sorting and managing mail deliveries, answering volunteer questions, coordinating supplies, and ensuring accurate data entry.

• Curate special student thank-you deliverables for our most impactful partners.

• Review incoming student thank-yous that have been escalated by volunteers to staff for further review.

• Connect with teachers and donors on tricky thank-yous that require an extra special touch.

• Welcome new volunteers. Respond to applications and schedule and run regular volunteer orientation sessions for new volunteers.

• Cultivate a fun, friendly, and productive volunteer environment. This keeps volunteers excited, inspired, and motivated to support our mission.

• Build relationships and a sense of community with (and between) our volunteers. You’ll make sure volunteers feel like an integral part of the DonorsChoose team.

• Contribute towards larger team initiatives, including supporting special projects. (25%)

• Collaborate on strategic initiatives and projects to support our team and the larger organization, as needed.

• For example, calling teachers in specific geographic areas to share relevant funding opportunities and encourage them to post classroom projects.

Qualifications

This position may be a fit for you if:

• You adapt quickly to changing priorities. You know how to roll with the punches, and are excited by change. You are cool and collected under pressure, are adaptable to meet team needs, and thrive in situations where you can help someone find a solution. You’re happy to jump in wherever needed.

• You live for organization, and pay attention to the details. You’re thorough, self-sufficient, and comfortable with repetitive, intricate tasks. You are meticulous when following instructions, and take pride in your attention to detail.

• You’re a natural relationship-builder and collaborator. You love forging authentic connections with others. You notice the person at the party who feels left out and immediately invite them to join the conversation - both online and IRL. Awkward silence? You don’t know what that is.

• You use good judgment in tricky situations. When guidelines don’t cover a situation, you consider how your decision will affect the donor experience.

• You are an A+ communicator. Your emails make people smile and you can explain just about anything to anyone.

• You are tech savvy. You’re comfortable with technology, and can learn new programs and tools quickly. (Our tech stack includes Google Workspace, Slack, Mailchimp, Zendesk, Salesforce).

• You are mission-motivated, and passionate about educational equity. You care about helping teachers, and believe that all students should have equal access to educational opportunities.

• You believe in the power of volunteerism - and have the experience to prove it. You have hands-on experience with working with volunteers or have been a volunteer yourself. You’ve already started jotting down potential ideas to engage our community.

Requirements

• One to two years of full-time work experience

• Available to work in person in our midtown Manhattan office 40 hours per week, Monday - Friday; also available to work:

• 12pm - 8pm one to two times per week

• On the weekends once or twice per month during peak season (September - February)

• Heavy lifting, approximately 25 pounds multiple times per day

Compensation & Benefits

The compensation for this role is $23.08 per hour. This is a non-exempt role and is eligible for overtime pay under the provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act.

Once employees are hired, everyone at DonorsChoose is eligible to receive annual performance-based raises as they grow in their role. We are open to a variety of experiences, and recognize that the person we hire may be less experienced or more senior than this job description as posted. If you don’t check every box listed here, or you know you’d bring additional experience to the table, we hope you’ll submit your application.

In addition, we offer full-time staff 25 paid vacation days per year and 11 paid holidays, a rich employer-paid individual and family health plan, a matching 401(k) plan (up to 5% of base salary), annual professional development stipend, and casual and flexible work environment. To learn more about what it is like to work for DonorsChoose, visit our careers page .

Other Details

DonorsChoose participates in E-Verify. We will provide the U.S. Social Security Administration (SSA) and, if necessary, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) with information from each new employee’s Form I-9 to confirm work authorization.

An important note on communications: All messages from our hiring team will come from an official @donorschoose.org email address. If you ever receive a message about a role with us from a different domain, it’s not from us, and you should not reply or click on any links. We care deeply about your time, your privacy, and your experience—thank you for your interest in joining the DonorsChoose mission!

DonorsChoose Core Values

EQUITY
Combating systemic inequity is crucial to a brighter future for all. This reality fuels our ambitions and drives us to persevere.

INGENUITY
Complex problems require innovative solutions. We dream big, get creative, roll up our sleeves, and take action. We believe the best products can change the world.

HUMANITY
People are the heart of our team and the communities we serve. Our compassion informs our goals and how we work together to achieve them.

INTEGRITY
We strive to do right. We’re up-front about the facts. We boldly learn and grow from mistakes.

LEARNING
Education is the beating heart of our organization, inside and out. We’re curious. We listen. We know we don’t know everything.

GRATITUDE
We begin and end with thanks. We take joy in our mission, our communities, and each other.

To Apply

Please submit your resume and answer the application questions online. Since we’re trying to get to know you through our hiring process, we ask that you please refrain from using AI writing tools to craft your response to our application questions. A cover letter is optional and may be addressed to Alexis Medina, Manager, Content Operations.

A Final Note

The DonorsChoose team works toward a nation where students in every community have the resources needed for an excellent education. To do this we hire and support a diverse team of the best and the brightest talent available because it makes us more effective, high-performing, creative and resilient.

If you are passionate about our mission, highly skilled in your field, and looking for a place where you can bring all of yourself to work, we want you.

Over the last 10+ years, Ellevation Education has built a thriving business serving the administrators, teachers, and specialists who support English Learners. Today, nearly 2,000 school districts use our software to manage their EL programs. We are a successful, growing business with a real mission: helping English Learners achieve their highest aspirations.
Districts across the country rely on Ellevation for the daily workflows that keep those programs running and the student data behind every instructional decision, and we earn that trust through what we build. We’re building a platform that is secure by design and fast to work on, and engineering practices that let eight squads ship with confidence. Much of that is still unbuilt. We want leaders who study how we work today, find the gaps we haven’t seen yet, and then design and build the systems, practices, and team that close them.
Ellevation operates as part of Curriculum Associates (“CA”) which provides several shared functions across all of its business units, including a centralized security organization. Ellevation runs its own R&D organization including engineering, product, and design; CA supplies scanning, security tooling, reporting, and KPIs.
Ellevation R&D spans engineering, product, and design, organized into eight product squads. Each squad owns its product area end to end and moves quickly within it. The work that spans squads, such as platform modernization, authentication, dependency currency, and security, needs deliberate ownership to move at the same pace.

About The Role
This is a senior role in R&D, and its impact reaches everything Ellevation builds. You’ll see across all eight squads, spot the problems and opportunities that sit where their work meets, and make a case for which of them matter most to the business. Platform modernization, authentication, dependency health, and security are where that work starts today, and you’ll shape what comes next.

You’ll lead a team of Staff Engineers who drive critical parts of this work, making the case for where their time goes and making sure every initiative has a clear owner, a plan the squads can work with, and an agreed outcome. We expect to grow the team over time, and you’ll shape and lead that hiring.

Your impact scales through your team. Our Staff Engineers work across squads, partnering with engineering managers and product leads to move shared work forward within real squad capacity. You'll help them choose the right problems, sequence work across the organization, and grow as technical leaders. You'll stay close enough to the technical detail to judge tradeoffs and stand behind your team's decisions.

Security is a core part of this portfolio, and we want a leader with meaningful security experience to own it. You'll lead security practice at Ellevation, working with CA on the standards, SLAs, and KPIs we're measured against and making sure Ellevation meets them. You'll also be a key liaison to CA's central security organization.

You’ll be accountable for the results of this work. That means weighing what should be fixed now, what can wait, and what isn’t worth doing, then recommending a path and explaining why it matters for the business. Security findings, CA’s standards, and Ellevation’s product priorities all compete for the same R&D time, and you’ll make the case for how to balance them. That includes making CA’s scanning, tooling, and reporting work for how Ellevation builds software, and representing Ellevation in CA’s security forums.

Deciding what to take on each cycle is a decision made among R&D leaders, and you are one of them. You bring the picture of technical and security risk that shapes what the group decides, and you're in the room when it's decided. You report to the VP of Engineering, who is an active partner and will engage where it counts, but you're expected to move things forward on your own.

What You'll Do
Drive cross-cutting bets

• Identify the problems that span squads, including platform modernization, authentication, dependency health, and security, and decide which are worth taking on

• Shape that work with Staff Engineers: define the problem, set boundaries on scope and time, and work through the technical risks before a team commits to it

• Bring shaped work to the group of R&D leaders, including you, who decide what teams take on each cycle, with a clear case for why it matters now

• Support the teams building cross-cutting work so they can make good technical decisions on their own

Lead the Staff Engineers

• Grow the Staff Engineer group through hiring and development, expanding the group’s capacity to drive impact across the business

• Set direction for the team and decide where each Staff Engineer's time goes, rebalancing as priorities shift

• Coach Staff Engineers as technical leaders: framing ambiguous problems, building agreement across squads, and writing decisions down

• Judge technical tradeoffs on cross-cutting work, and stand behind your team's decisions

Lead security practice at Ellevation

• Turn the standards agreed with CA into working practice at Ellevation, with clear ownership and escalation inside engineering

• Get findings into the tools and workflows engineers already use, in a form they can act on without interpretation

• Build security thinking, such as threat modeling, into how work is shaped

• Coordinate the full security surface with CA's teams, including incident response, vendor and third-party risk, security awareness, district security questionnaires, and pen test cycles

• Hold accountability for Ellevation's compliance evidence, coordinating contributions across engineering and product

Own the CA security relationship

• Own Ellevation's relationship with CA's central security organization, and learn how security decisions get made there

• Work with CA on the standards, SLAs, and KPIs Ellevation is measured against: understand how they're set and calculated, help shape how they apply to Ellevation, and push for changes where they don't fit how we build

• Partner with CA on how its central scanning is scoped and configured for Ellevation's repositories and stack

• Reconcile Ellevation's reporting with CA's so nobody is surprised by a number

• Report weekly to CA stakeholders on remediation progress, blockers, and security KPIs

• Represent Ellevation in CA security forums, and bring back what's relevant in a form Ellevation can act on

What You'll Bring
• 10+ years in software engineering, including experience leading engineering teams

• Experience hiring and leading senior and staff-level engineers, and growing them as technical leaders

• A track record of taking large, ambiguous technical problems that span teams, such as platform modernization, legacy migrations, or authentication, from a well-defined problem through delivery, working through teams that did not report to you

• A strong technical foundation in modern web applications, cloud infrastructure, and CI/CD, enough to judge tradeoffs and earn credibility with Staff Engineers

• A background in security across application security, cloud security, compliance, and incident response, including hands-on experience with SAST, SCA, and dependency scanning tooling

• Experience moving decisions forward in a matrixed organization, ideally between a central function and a business unit at a parent company, acquirer, or major partner

• A track record of communicating technical and security risk to executive audiences

• Experience building software that handles sensitive or regulated data, such as in education, healthcare, or financial services, is a strong plus

• Ability to provide care 2 evenings per week (meaning being available until 8pm in your patient caseloads primary time zone).

• Ability to safely and effectively deliver care in a virtual setting.

• Passion for mental health and eating disorder treatment and expanding access to treatment.

• Experience in Family-Based Treatment and/or eating disorder treatment.

• Proven track record of meeting goals.

The global supply chain is one of the most heavily regulated industries for all parties involved. Everyone from the carriers, intermediaries, trucking companies, 3rd party logistics, freight forwarders, shippers, consignees, importers, exporters, and brokers face a challenging and complex task of navigating through a myriad of laws from the originating country, destination country as well as international treaties and conventions.

The Trade Advisory team, consisting of business consultants, lawyers and licensed customs brokers, offers advanced customs and trade expertise to help clients identify supply chain risks and cost savings opportunities. We are looking for a Trade Advisory Associate - Entry Audit to join our Trade Advisory team. This team member will work closely with the Trade Advisory Lead to execute client entry audit projects, managing the day-to-day work associated with each engagement from data intake through final reporting and recommendations.

Audit scope: Entry audits review a client's historical import entries to validate compliance and uncover risk and savings opportunities. Scope typically includes tariff classification, customs valuation, country of origin, duty rates and special program eligibility (including free trade agreements and additional tariff programs), antidumping and countervailing duty exposure, and the accuracy of entry data filed in ACE. Findings are quantified, documented, and translated into corrective actions such as prior disclosures, post summary corrections, and duty refund or recovery opportunities.

• Build and maintain Excel models and workbooks to map data from ACE to client specific business rules.

• Design, build, and maintain automated workflows and data pipelines using N8N, Parabola, or equivalent tools to streamline audit analysis and reporting.

• Identify discrepancies, quantify duty and fee impact, and document audit findings with supporting evidence.

• Prepare clear audit reports and client-ready summaries of findings, root causes, and recommended corrective actions.

• Support remediation efforts resulting from audit findings, such as post summary corrections, prior disclosures, and refund or recovery filings.

• Ensure project timelines, statuses, and invoices are appropriately managed and delivered.

• Maintain active communication with clients, customs and other government authorities, and internal stakeholders, elevating issues where necessary.

An overview of this role

As a SLED Solutions Architect, you'll be a trusted technical advisor to State, Local, and Education customers in every state east of the Mississippi River: state agencies, counties, cities, special districts, community colleges, and public, private, and research universities. These organizations deliver services residents and students rely on every day, often with lean IT teams, aging systems, fixed fiscal-year budgets, and growing cybersecurity threats.

You'll show them how GitLab's DevSecOps platform and AI capabilities, including the GitLab Duo Agent Platform, help them modernize legacy applications, protect sensitive resident and student data, meet state and sector compliance requirements, and do more with the staff they have. You'll own the technical evaluation and validation stages of the sales cycle, guide customers through proofs of concept and value, and translate platform capabilities into outcomes that agency leaders, CIOs, CISOs, and procurement officers can defend in a budget request or an RFP evaluation.

You'll partner closely with SLED account executives, channel partners, and systems integrators, provide technical guidance from first conversation through successful deployment, and bring the voice of the SLED customer back into Product, Sales, and Marketing.

Location and travel: The territory covers all states east of the Mississippi River. The candidate must reside in the Northeast part of the United States. This role requires up to 50% travel.

What you'll do

• Engage SLED customers onsite and remotely, from state capitals to university campuses, with tailored demos, technical presentations, and hands-on workshops that tie GitLab to their mission.

• Partner with SLED account executives to shape account strategies that align with each customer's fiscal year budget cycle, legislative appropriations, IT modernization plans, and grant or federal pass through funding.

• Own the technical evaluation process, including proof of concept (POC) and proof of value (POV) design and delivery, and provide technical responses for RFIs, RFPs, RFQs, and security questionnaires.

• Support purchases made through cooperative purchasing agreements and statewide contract vehicles by working with channel and reseller partners.

• Guide customers through state and sector security requirements, such as GovRAMP and NIST frameworks, and show how GitLab's built in security, auditability, and deployment options reduce compliance burden.

• Help agencies and institutions modernize legacy and mainframe applications, such as unemployment insurance, tax, DMV, benefits, and student information systems, using GitLab and AI-assisted development to lower risk and offset shrinking pools of legacy skilled staff.

• Advise customers on adopting AI responsibly, including the GitLab Duo Agent Platform, in line with state AI policies, governance boards, and data privacy requirements.

• Lead the creation of Customer Success Plans that capture technical success criteria and handoff details, ensuring a smooth path to deployment and adoption, often for IT teams with limited capacity.

• Work alongside Account Executives to build data driven business cases that quantify delivery bottlenecks, giving customers a defensible basis for budget requests and clear evidence of return on taxpayer investment.

• Build relationships with CIOs, CISOs, agency directors, enterprise architects, faculty, research computing leaders, and procurement officers so they become advocates for GitLab, including across agencies and campuses that share services.

• Collaborate with systems integrators and state IT shared-services organizations to scale GitLab adoption across multiple agencies, local governments, or campuses.

• Serve as the SLED customer advocate internally, channeling feedback on procurement, compliance, and deployment needs to Product, Sales, and Marketing.

• Stay current on GitLab and related technologies, and create reusable SLED demos, reference architectures, and assets for customers and partners.

What you'll bring

• Background in technical pre-sales, consulting, or IT roles serving state agencies, local governments, or public, private, and research universities, where you guided customers through evaluations and solution design.

• Working knowledge of how SLED organizations buy technology: RFP and RFI cycles, cooperative purchasing agreements, statewide contracts, fiscal-year budgeting, and the role of resellers and systems integrators.

• Hands-on experience using GitLab and familiarity with modern software development and operations practices, such as CI/CD, DevSecOps, and automation.

• Experience with cloud, hybrid, and self-managed deployments in regulated environments, including government cloud regions, and an understanding of data residency and sovereignty concerns.

• Familiarity with security and compliance frameworks common in SLED, such as GovRAMP and NIST SP 800-53.

• Ability to connect technical solutions to mission outcomes, such as resident service delivery, cyber resilience, cost avoidance, and workforce efficiency, and to advise senior stakeholders on tradeoffs and options.

• Strong communication and relationship-building skills, including presenting to both technical teams and non-technical leaders such as agency heads, procurement officers, and university administrators.

• Openness to learning, seeking feedback, and building new skills, including familiarity with GitLab's Solutions Architect handbook and related resources.

Nice to have

• Prior experience working in or for state or local government IT, or a university IT or research computing organization.

• Experience with legacy or mainframe modernization programs.

• Familiarity with AI governance practices in the public sector, such as AI use-case inventories, acceptable-use policies, and risk assessments.

About the team

The SLED Solutions Architect role is part of GitLab's Public Sector Solutions Architect team, a group of trusted technical advisors who help government and education customers understand, evaluate, and adopt the GitLab DevSecOps platform. The team is distributed and collaborates asynchronously across time zones using GitLab and our handbook-first practices to share knowledge, reusable examples, and best practices.

On the SLED team, you'll help customers solve challenges unique to state, local, and education organizations: protecting resident and student data, modernizing mission-critical legacy systems, buying through public procurement processes, and stretching limited IT staff and budgets. Senior Manager, Support Engineering (U.S. Government)

An overview of this role

As a Senior Manager, Support Engineering on our U.S. Government support team, you’ll co-lead a team of engineers supporting complex enterprise deployments in highly regulated environments. You’ll combine people-focused leadership, technical judgment, and business acumen to develop engineers, strengthen our support program, and help customers realize value from GitLab.

You’ll also connect the team’s technical contributions to outcomes that matter across the business. This includes telling a compelling, evidence-based story about how Support Engineering helps protect revenue, enable growth, remove barriers to adoption, and accelerate customer time to value. You’ll help executives and sales teams understand the significance of the work engineers perform and how that work supports customer and organizational success.

Beyond individual cases, you’ll recognize Support Engineering as a valuable source of business intelligence. By bringing together engineers’ firsthand observations, product trends, and recurring customer pain points, you’ll turn field signal into actionable insights for Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success.

What you’ll do

• Co-lead, coach, and develop a team of Support Engineers, building a culture of trust, accountability, technical excellence, and customer-focused decision-making.

• Drive hiring, onboarding, performance management, and career development, helping engineers build technical expertise, communication skills, and an understanding of their broader business impact.

• Partner with other Support Engineering Managers to shape program strategy, establish priorities, plan capacity, and evolve processes and tooling as customer and business needs change.

• Translate complex technical work into clear, compelling narratives for executives and sales teams, connecting engineers’ contributions to revenue protection, growth opportunities, customer adoption, and faster time to value.

• Use operational data, customer context, and qualitative feedback to evaluate support effectiveness, communicate impact, and guide investment and improvement decisions.

• Establish a repeatable approach to capturing engineers’ insights and identifying product trends, recurring customer pain points, adoption barriers, and emerging government requirements.

• Partner with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success to turn support intelligence into actionable recommendations for product improvements, enablement, and customer engagement.

• Maintain technical engagement by joining customer calls, reviewing tickets, and helping engineers navigate complex or sensitive issues, while developing the team’s ability to resolve challenges independently.

• Coordinate responses to escalated and critical customer situations during working hours, providing clear communication and sound judgment.

• Champion improvements that address recurring problems, reduce customer friction, and strengthen the quality and scalability of our U.S. Government support offering.

What you’ll bring

• Demonstrated success leading and developing technical support or engineering teams, including coaching, performance management, career development, and leadership through growth and change.

• A strong technical background supporting complex enterprise software or infrastructure, with the ability to assess technical challenges, recognize the value engineers deliver, and understand the implications for customer outcomes.

• Experience translating technical accomplishments into business value for executive and sales audiences, using clear storytelling supported by data and customer context.

• Business acumen to connect support outcomes with revenue protection, customer retention, growth, product adoption, and time to value.

• The ability to treat engineers’ knowledge and customer interactions as sources of business intelligence, synthesizing individual observations into meaningful trends and actionable recommendations.

• Experience setting priorities, planning resources, and improving support programs while balancing immediate customer needs with longer-term organizational goals.

• A people-focused leadership approach that builds trust, encourages candid feedback, recognizes contributions, and creates opportunities for engineers to grow.

• Experience managing high-severity incidents and sensitive escalations, including effective communication with customers, executives, and cross-functional stakeholders.

• The ability to influence across Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success, building alignment around customer needs and shared business outcomes.

• Familiarity with U.S. Government customers and the operational, security, and regulatory constraints that shape their environments. We also welcome candidates with relevant experience in other complex or regulated industries.

Our U.S. Government Support team formed in 2019 and has grown alongside the adoption of GitLab within government agencies. We help customers troubleshoot complex environments and use GitLab’s DevSecOps platform securely and effectively.

Distributed across the United States, we combine synchronous and asynchronous collaboration to support customers and build strong working relationships in a remote-first environment. Our team includes both tenured and newer engineers, bringing diverse technical experience and perspectives.

We’re focused on developing our people, scaling our operations, strengthening crisis management for sensitive systems, and deepening our partnerships across GitLab. As a senior leader, you’ll help make the team’s technical expertise and customer knowledge more valuable to the broader organization, while ensuring engineers have the support, direction, and development opportunities they need to succeed.

An overview of this role

As a Staff Product Manager on the Tenant Scale area within Infrastructure Platforms, you’ll set product direction for how GitLab supports large, complex customers as they grow across departments, projects, and regions. This role focuses on the product choices needed to make tenant data more portable, scalable, and ready for a unified deployment model across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and, over time, Self-Managed. You’ll work on problems that sit at the intersection of product strategy, infrastructure, and customer needs, including how we build a platform to horizontally scale our SaaS architecture, how to enable tenant movement between environments, how isolation and regional requirements are handled, and what needs to be in place to support a more cellular architecture.

At the Staff level, your scope extends beyond a single group. Your direction will inform the broader Infrastructure Platforms direction, you’ll make the investment case for unified deployment capabilities, and you’ll be a recognized authority, inside and outside GitLab, on multi-tenant and cellular SaaS architecture. In your first year, you’ll partner closely with engineering and product peers to define requirements, drive alignment, and move this work from concept into a deployment model teams can build on, while coaching fellow product managers as they pick up work from the shared pool.

What you’ll do

• Drive product strategy and direction for tenant scale and unified deployment capabilities across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and future deployment models, informing the broader Infrastructure Platforms direction and moving this work from concept into a deployment model teams can build on in your first year.

• Set quarterly and annual plans for tenant portability and platform unification, breaking large epics into issues and minimal valuable changes (MVCs) and practicing iteration across multiple groups.

• Define requirements for our unified deployment platform, including the capabilities needed before tenants can be hosted in a unified deployment unit.

• Partner closely with engineering counterparts and highly technical teams to turn infrastructure constraints and platform needs into clear product direction.

• Collaborate with product peers across the platforms organization, including teams working on GitLab.com and adjacent infrastructure areas, and manage with influence to align work that spans more than one group.

• Engage with internal and external customers to understand needs related to isolation, regional deployment, compliance, and operational readiness, using qualitative interviews to find patterns and sharpen problem statements.

• Build business cases for investment in tenant scale and unified deployment, including build, buy, and partner options, the cost of isolation, regionality, and compliance, and the expected benefits.

• Facilitate tradeoff discussions around scalability, tenant encapsulation, deployment consistency, and platform unification, and escalate cleanly to the right level of leadership when decisions or progress are blocked.

• Translate complex technical concepts into product plans, priorities, and documentation that align distributed teams on delivery milestones for tenant portability and platform unification, using error budgets and other performance indicators to inform direction.

• Represent GitLab as a trusted voice on cellular architecture and tenant scale in customer calls, events, and other external forums.

• Coach fellow product managers on direction updates, customer validation, and GitLab’s architecture and tech stack, and support a collaborative team model where product managers share ownership across a common pool of work and step into the areas where they can have the most impact.

What you’ll bring

• Experience managing product work in technical domains such as infrastructure, scalability, platform architecture, software delivery, or cloud services, with results delivered across a range of product areas rather than a single one.

• Ability to work effectively with deeply technical engineering teams and build credibility in discussions about system design, deployment models, and platform constraints.

• Knowledge of how SaaS or platform-based systems scale, including concepts such as multitenancy, horizontal scalability, autoscaling, workload isolation, and production readiness, and the ability to build a deep understanding of GitLab’s architecture and tech stack and coach others on it.

• Comfort working with customers or internal stakeholders on complex requirements, including operational, compliance, or regional deployment needs.

• Skill in turning ambiguous technical problems into clear product strategy, quarterly and annual plans, priorities, and actionable work.

• Expertise in qualitative customer interviewing and product validation, with the ability to teach those techniques to others.

• Experience building business cases, including weighing build, buy, and partner options and forecasting benefits against the competitive landscape.

• Experience collaborating across product, engineering, user experience, and other cross-functional partners in a distributed environment, using iteration and influence to raise the performance of peers beyond your own group.

• Strength in clear written and verbal communication, especially when explaining complex infrastructure topics to different audiences, with excellent presentation skills at every level of the company.

• Recognition as a thought leader in a relevant domain, internally and externally, for example through speaking, writing, or representing your company at customer events and conferences.

• Openness to candidates who bring transferable experience from engineering, technical support, or adjacent product roles relevant to large-scale platforms.

About the team

The team sits within Infrastructure Platforms and works on foundational platform capabilities. It partners closely with engineering, adjacent product managers, and internal customers across regions, with a strong emphasis on GitLab’s asynchronous working style and long-term platform thinking. Product managers on the team share ownership of a common pool of work; at the Staff level, you’ll help guide how that work is prioritized and mentor teammates as they take it on.

An overview of this role

As a Senior Corporate Security Engineer, you'll help secure the systems GitLab team members rely on every day across a fully remote environment. This role sits within Corporate Security Engineering and focuses on building secure-by-default controls for endpoints and the SaaS platforms that support them, with a strong emphasis on macOS. You'll own meaningful technical decisions around endpoint hardening, automation, and detection, and you'll help turn security requirements into scalable engineering systems that are measurable, auditable, and designed to reduce friction for end users.

This is a strong fit if you're motivated by solving security problems with code. You will work across endpoint management, identity, and security operations to improve how GitLab manages macOS, iOS, Windows, and Linux devices through Infrastructure-as-Code, Terraform, and GitOps workflows. In your first year, you'll be expected to strengthen endpoint security architecture, expand automation, and improve the reliability and auditability of how controls are deployed and maintained.

What you’ll do

• Help lead the security architecture of GitLab's endpoint fleet and related infrastructure, with a primary focus on macOS.

• Design and support automation for secure endpoint deployment, configuration, and lifecycle management using code-based workflows.

• Manage endpoint and SaaS security configuration through Terraform, version control, merge requests, continuous integration pipelines, and automated rollouts.

• Define and enforce security baselines across macOS, iOS, Windows, and Linux endpoints.

• Develop patching and software distribution approaches that align with security, compliance, and operational requirements.

• Partner with Information Technology, Security Operations, and Detection and Response teams to improve endpoint telemetry, detections, and response models.

• Drive process improvements that reduce manual work and lower risk by favoring automation, policy-driven controls, and auditable change management.

• Mentor engineers across Corporate Security and Information Technology, and serve as a senior escalation point for complex endpoint security issues.

What you’ll bring

• Experience designing and delivering endpoint, systems, or corporate security solutions in environments that require scalable, durable controls.

• Deep knowledge of endpoint management platforms such as Jamf Pro or FleetDM, especially for architecting and securing macOS environments.

• Strong hands-on ability with Terraform and Infrastructure-as-Code practices, including module design, state management, and pipeline-based deployment.

• Experience working with GitOps workflows where changes are managed through Git repositories, merge requests, code review, and automated pipelines.

• Strong proficiency in scripting or programming for automation and security tooling, such as bash, Python, PowerShell, or Go.

• Familiarity with cloud identity providers and directories, including platforms such as Okta, Google Workspace, LDAP.

• Ability to communicate clearly, collaborate across distributed teams, and work independently in an all-remote environment.

• Openness to bringing transferable experience from adjacent security, systems, or platform engineering backgrounds, along with a practical and security-focused approach to problem solving.

About the team

The Corporate Security Engineering team secures the internal environment GitLab team members use every day, including endpoints, identity systems, SaaS applications, and platforms that store sensitive internal data. It's a small, high-leverage team that treats security work as engineering work: building with code, operating through Git, and using reviewable, testable, and auditable workflows by default. The team partners closely with Information Technology, Security Operations, and Engineering across regions, collaborating asynchronously to build controls that scale across GitLab's all-remote workforce while reducing friction for end users.

1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

Headway is a ~$750M net revenue business growing ~70% year over year. We serve three customers (patients, providers and payers) across a fast-growing set of teams and initiatives. As we scale, the quality of our decisions, operating rhythms, and cross-functional execution are incredibly important and are becoming increasingly complex.

We are looking for a Head of Strategy & Operations, Office of the COO to partner closely with our COO, Rob Sadow. You'll serve as the COO’s right hand and point of leverage — running the company’s core operating processes, turning the company's most important priorities into action, strengthening how the executive team operates, and ensuring critical decisions and initiatives move forward with clarity and accountability.

This is a high-trust, high-impact, senior leader, individual contributor role reporting directly to the COO, with significant exposure to the executive team and the broader business.

You'll also work closely with the COO's Executive Assistant to ensure his time and attention are focused on the decisions and priorities that matter most.

What you’ll own in partnership with the COO

• Key company operating processes. Planning, OKRs, other important operating cadences. Keep each one lightweight and automate everything that doesn't need human judgment.

• Company execution. Own the weekly company OKR review and what comes out of it. When something looks off, go to the source: pull the data, join the conversation or call the meeting. Come back with a diagnosis, a recommendation and a named owner.

• The decision queue. Be the first stop for decisions that would otherwise go to the COO. Make the calls within agreed decision rights and send back what belongs with functional owners. Bring him the rest with options, a recommendation and a deadline, and make sure every decision leaves with an owner and a resolution date.

• Critical initiatives without a clear owner: Resolve new, high-stakes, cross-functional problems that would otherwise land on the COO's desk. Define the problem, align the stakeholders, and drive it to resolution or hand it to a permanent owner.

• Org health and productivity: In partnership with the HRBP and Finance teams, you’ll be one step ahead to ensure the org structure grows in alignment with the business. From supporting the scoping and hiring of key roles to making sure staffing ratios are aligned with talent competitors.

You’d be a great fit if...

• You’ve operated at an executive level and owned the outcome, as a COO or Head of Operations at an earlier-stage company, or as a VP, Senior Director of Strategy & Operations, or GM at a larger one. You can point to the results you were accountable for.

• You’ve run a company-wide process end to end, such as annual or quarterly planning, goal-setting, or business reviews. You can tell which parts of a process create clarity and which just add overhead, and you’ve cut the latter.

• You’ve worked directly with a CEO, COO, or executive team at a company that at least doubled in revenue while you were there. You’ve been trusted to attend meetings in an executive’s place and make decisions on their behalf.

• You’ve hired senior people through a rigorous process and built or rebuilt a team. You hold a high bar and can describe a candidate you passed on who was good but not great.

• You’re strategic with a demonstrated ability to break down a problem to its parts and push the team’s thinking to deliver a vision and execution plan.

• You’re an exceptional writer who can boil a complicated, high-stakes issue down to one page that makes the trade-off and the recommendation clear.

• You quickly figure out what matters in a messy situation. You go straight to the people and data closest to the problem, form a point of view, and bring options with a clear recommendation.

• You’ve owned board or investor materials, including the narrative and analysis behind them.

• You use AI and automation to take manual work out of a process rather than adding people to it.

Prior Chief of Staff experience, consulting experience, and an MBA are all welcome, but none are required.

Headway is deploying hundreds of millions in capital across two growth engines — provider acquisition and patient acquisition. On the one hand, the two engines are economically distinct — different funnels, different metrics, different payback profiles. On the other hand, there are deeply interrelated components between the motions that (1) make the Headway marketplace work and (2) drive our ability to build a better mental healthcare system that everyone can access.

We're looking for a Director of GTM Finance to drive our financial decision making for these two growth engines. You're responsible for capital deployment, evaluating our return on investment, and helping our business leaders make good growth decisions. Ultimately your work is a critical enabler to helping providers find Headway and patients find high quality care.

What You'll Own

• The revenue model and forecast. Own Headway's revenue model end to end – the driver-based architecture connecting providers, patients, funnel conversion, retention, and utilization to booked revenue.

• Capital allocation and unit economics. Facilitate smart capital allocation decisions across provider growth and patient growth, through deep understanding of CAC, LTV, payback, and channel level performance.

• Planning and capacity. Run annual planning and monthly forecasting across GTM functions. You own GTM headcount, ramp, and capacity planning in partner with business leadership.

• Team and function building. Hire, coach, and grow a high-impact GTM Finance team. Set the analytical bar, define roles and DRIs, and build the infrastructure the function runs on – models, dashboards, agentic workflows, and reporting alongside the Data team.

• You've owned the forecast and capital deployment for a growth business operating at meaningful scale.

• You know growth economics cold, and you're obsessed with what's underneath the average. Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!).

Principles that guide us:

• Focus on the mission: We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapists to better solve the problems they're facing.

• Ship small, learn fast: We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iterating.

• Everything is a product: Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind.

• Vulnerability Management: Snyk, Semgrep

About the Role:

The best SDETs in the industry are no longer measured by how many tests they write. They're measured by the systems they build that decide whether software is safe to ship — and, increasingly, by how well they wield AI to do it.

That's the role we're hiring for. We're looking for a Senior Staff SDET to own quality architecture and engineering strategy for our most critical systems, and to lead how we apply AI across our entire testing and release pipeline. You'll build the frameworks, platforms, and agent-driven workflows that the rest of engineering depends on, define what "safe to ship" means here, and stay deep in the code while doing it.

This is a genuinely hands-on senior technical leadership role with impact that spans many teams. If you want to build AI-native quality systems rather than bolt AI tools onto a legacy suite, this is that job.

Why This Role Is Different

• AI is the core of the work. You'll own how we use LLMs and agents for test generation, failure triage, self-healing, and release decisioning — and you'll set the guardrails that keep it trustworthy.

• You'll test AI, not just test with it. We ship AI-powered product features, which means building evaluation harnesses, golden datasets, and probabilistic assertions for systems that don't return the same answer twice. This is frontier work with very little established playbook.

We are looking for an experienced mental health clinician and leader with a passion for clinical care, quality, and management to serve as a clinical quality supervisor for our Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) Program, an evidence-based treatment for borderline personality disorder, suicidal and self-harm behaviors, and emotion regulation difficulties. Lyra offers comprehensive DBT for both adults (aged 18+) and adolescents (aged 13-17). Both the adult and adolescent DBT programs involve weekly individual therapy, weekly DBT skills training groups, and weekly consultation team meetings for DBT therapists. All Lyra DBT clients also have 24/7 access to a team of licensed clinicians who have been trained in DBT skills coaching for around the clock support.
As a DBT Clinical Quality Supervisor, you will spend half the time delivering direct client care to DBT clients and half the time providing management oversight and clinical consultation to a team of DBT therapists.
Direct client care: You will provide DBT for adolescents and adults via telehealth. You’ll provide individual DBT, multifamily skills groups, and parenting and family sessions for adolescents and their parents, as well as individual DBT and DBT skills groups for adult clients. You’ll also assign DBT-relevant digital lessons, videos, and assessments to your clients to enhance learnings and monitor outcomes between sessions. An important note: Clients come from a multitude of different backgrounds and experiences, and have varying needs and abilities. We strive to continue to meet their unique needs by delivering culturally responsive care–an approach that accounts for the impact of cultural backgrounds on each person’s care experience.
Clinical management: You will provide management oversight of and clinical consultation and training to a team of DBT therapists delivering care to clients through our innovative video therapy platform. This includes reviewing and providing feedback on clinical quality metrics and consulting on clinical cases. You will also assist with quality improvement initiatives, including leading consultation teams, provider training, and quality assurance reviews.
Regularly: Our DBT team members enjoy connecting with peers, who share a passion for providing evidence-based care. You’ll attend DBT clinical consultation team meetings and robust training to enhance your clinical and management skills. You’ll always have access to expert consultation and support for your most complex clients. It’s like a safety net of resources to help plan the best options–from specialty consultations to culturally responsive care–you’re not alone, even while working remotely within the US.
This role is a great fit if you have experience providing comprehensive DBT to adolescents and adults, a commitment to evidence-based and culturally responsive care and clinical quality assurance, and experience in administrative and clinical management of licensed independent mental health providers and developing high performing teams.

Provide clinical coverage for DBT individual, family, and group sessions as needed

Other duties as assigned

We are looking for a full-timeNeurodiversity Navigator who is passionate about whole-person, whole-family mental health care to join our clinical team. This remote position reports to the Supervisor, Neurodiversity Navigation.

As a Neurodiversity Navigator, you’ll be doing the important and meaningful work of supporting individuals as they navigate through the complex landscape of care for neurodiversity. You will provide critical psychoeducation on topics like early intervention services, behavioral strategies to address neurodiversity-related needs, navigating a diagnosis, and how to advocate for school, government and workplace accommodation services. Additionally, you will help connect clients to high-quality, evidence-based diagnosticians, services, and providers, depending on their needs. The focus of this role includes (but is not limited to) providing support to caregivers of children/adolescents with suspected or diagnosed neurodiverse conditions, supporting adults seeking neuroaffirming and neurodiversity-informed care, and assisting clients with navigating assessment services and support resources. This position does not involve in-person services or therapy, but rather provides support to individuals and families related to neurodiversity via phone, video conference, and/or email.

Responsibilities
• Support clients by understanding their current situation, conducting a brief assessment related to needs and potential risk concerns, providing psychoeducation relevant to the client and their needs, creating a client-centered care plan, and connecting the client to treatment or support options and resources.

Use an assessment rubric to determine whether neuropsychological testing is indicated for a given Lyra member, based on history, presenting concerns, and other factors. If testing is recommended, you will also help to assess whether a member is appropriate for virtual or in-person neuropsychological testing.

•
Administer psychoeducational training to caregivers of children/teens with neurodiverse conditions in order to help them learn skills to address behavior and neurodiversity-related needs, as well as to improve caregiving strategies.

•
Serve as a neurodiversity subject matter expert—providing guidance on how to best handle situations involving neurodiverse needs, consulting with cross-functional and clinical teams regarding best practices in the context of neurodiversity, and contributing to establishing strong provider partnerships.

•
Independently manage a caseload of complex, multi-need, neurodiverse clients , providing collaborative case management.

•
Successfully facilitate ongoing engagement, supporting clients as they move through various levels of care, employing neuroaffirming strategies to support client readiness for treatment.

•
Manage client crises, providing brief risk and needs assessments, and connecting the client to treatment or crisis resources when needed.

•
Respond to in-the-moment callers seeking crisis support, offering brief, evidence-based coping skills.

•
Effectively and professionally communicate with clients and providers throughout the process of accessing care, via modalities such as email, phone, care portal/EHR, and videoconferencing.

•
Creatively troubleshoot roadblocks to offering personalized, high quality clinical care options for our clients.

•
Use Lyra’s proprietary matching software, as well as other methods including facility database, health plan directory, and internet searches to identify treatment options for clients, and connect clients to the evidence-based treatment options, based on each individual client’s specific needs and preferences.

•
During caregiver training, administer and monitor measures to assess overall caregiver strain and stress.

•
Participate in and present cases for discussion in multidisciplinary clinical consultation team meetings, when needed.

•
Coordinate care and communicate with clients’ health plans, billing team, and/or clinical and support teams.

• Provide feedback to leadership for continuous program improvement, including suggestions to improve client experience, operational efficiencies, or outcomes.

•
Master’s degree Board Certified Behavior Analyst; BCBA certification and/or independent licensure is required. We’re unable to provide supervised hours toward licensure.

•
Significant experience managing neurodiversity-related clinical situations (preference towards experience providing case management expertise)

•
Experience providing training and/or education regarding behavior and neurodiversity-related topics to caregivers and/or clients

Deep understanding of the neurodiversity care navigation landscape at the national, state, and regional levels, for both children and adults

Comfort in environments with constantly evolving responsibilities

Passion for connecting individuals with excellent client-centered care and ability to provide short-term support via phone, videoconferencing, and email

Conduct comprehensive behavioral health assessments and develop individualized treatment plans.

Collaborate with psychiatrists, behavioral case managers, coaches, nurses, and other interdisciplinary team members to provide coordinated care.

Ability to meet applicable state licensing, credentialing, payer enrollment requirements, and interstate practice requirements.

Experience providing evidence-based behavioral health treatment to children, adolescents, young adults, and families.

Strong clinical judgment with excellent communication, organization, and documentation skills.

Tech-savvy and comfortable utilizing telehealth platforms, electronic health records, and other digital tools to deliver high-quality virtual care.

Warm, engaging, and collaborative clinical style with the ability to build therapeutic rapport across developmental stages.

Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions currently land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. As our customer base and billing complexity have grown, these cases take too long, repeat for the same reasons, and pull CSMs away from adoption and renewal work. As the Contract and Billing Resolution Specialist, you will be the single owner of complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.

You will take a customer's report that something is wrong with their bill, work out what happened across systems and teams, choose the right path to fix it, and see it through, keeping the customer informed. It is part detective, part project manager, part customer advocate. You will also tell the teams who own the underlying systems and processes what keeps breaking.

Your role will be cross-functional, working alongside and connecting Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal. This is a new role, and you will help shape the case record, the root-cause tags, and the monthly read-out that define how Customer Success resolves billing and contract cases at Samsara.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You should apply if:

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.

• You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.

• You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.

• You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.

• You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will:

• Own complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts, from the first report to a confirmed fix, and keep the customer informed in plain terms, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension.

• Reconstruct the full story behind a billing error across contracts, order forms, segment or ownership changes, reprocessing, and invoicing, including cases with several AE handoffs and no clean record of what was promised.

• Separate a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and choose the path that fixes the customer's billing, not only the immediate complaint.

• Drive Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal to execute the fix.

• Evaluate and prepare concession requests: confirm whether Samsara was at fault, size the request against policy and the approval matrix, write a short case summary (what happened, root cause, options considered and ruled out, recommendation, and risk), route it to the right approver, and confirm the credit is applied and the customer told.

• Support cancellation, return, and ETF exceptions: validate eligibility (purchase and renewal dates, trial history, Return ACV, financing partner, documentation), prepare the case for the approving team, act as the Customer Success fallback when the first approver does not respond within the window, and make sure approved outcomes are processed.

• Be the front door for billing, concession, and cancellation requests: log every request in a single case record, including those that arrive via Slack, email, or Gainsight; redirect them to the right path; and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.

• Fix repeat causes: tag the root cause on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved.

• Carry forward the billing improvement work with Support, Finance, and Product, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.

• Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.

Minimum requirements for the role:

• 4+ years of experience in billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, deal desk, contracts, or a similar finance and operations role.

• This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence.

• Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, including when the people involved have left.

• Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.

• Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.

• A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including working to deadlines in an approval process.

• Familiarity with order forms, amendments, and terms, and how they flow into billing.

• Comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent, and rigorous case management so nothing drops across weeks and stakeholders.

• Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues.

An ideal candidate also has:

• Experience handling escalated or high-dollar billing disputes.

• Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, or an equivalent ERP, and CPQ tools. We also use Zendesk, Gainsight, and Sweethawk.

• Customer Success, Support, or account management background with customer-facing financial or contract work.

• Experience building or improving billing dispute processes.

• Exposure to subscription or hardware-plus-subscription billing.

• AI First: Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes.

• Strong bias for action and insistence on high standards

As a Security Operations Engineer at Samsara, you will join a global team dedicated to protecting our people, systems, and information. You will triage and investigate security alerts, run incident response efforts, and help improve the tools, runbooks, and automated workflows we use to detect and respond to threats.

This role is an ideal next step if you have built foundational experience in a SOC or hands-on security environment and want to develop your technical craft. At Samsara, we view this level as a collaborative apprenticeship: you will develop independent execution skills on discrete investigations, break down incoming alerts into actionable steps, partner with incident stakeholders to remediate findings, and work alongside experienced responders during complex security incidents. You will also explore modern AI tools and insights to simplify routine tasks and optimize your day-to-day workflow.

We are looking for someone who follows the evidence, communicates with intellectual honesty, asks thoughtful questions, and brings a collaborative, pragmatic approach to security operations.

This is a remote position open to candidates based in the United States and in the Pacific Timezone.

You should apply if:

• You enjoy investigating: You like working through unfamiliar activity, connecting evidence from different sources, and explaining what happened.

• You want to improve how security operates: You notice repetitive work, unclear instructions or noisy alerts and want to help make them better.

• You want to develop your craft: You’re looking for hands-on responsibility, feedback from experienced colleagues, and opportunities to grow across incident response and automation.

• You want your work to have real-world impact: You’re motivated by helping protect the technology behind industries that keep the world moving and help workers return home safely.

In this role, you will:

• Monitor, triage and investigate security alerts across identity, endpoint, email, SaaS and cloud environments, using our tools, runbooks and escalation procedures.

• Own routine investigations and incidents through to a documented outcome: gather evidence, establish a timeline, assess the activity and explain your conclusions.

• Support experienced responders during major security incidents through evidence collection, technical analysis, and agreed containment and recovery actions.

• Maintain clear investigation records and provide useful updates and handovers to teammates across regions.

• Improve runbooks, help tune detections, and contribute small scripts or automated workflows with guidance and review from teammates.

• Participate in post-incident reviews and turn lessons learned into practical improvements.

• Champion Samsara’s cultural principles: Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, and Win as a Team.

Minimum requirements for the role:

• Hands-on experience triaging and investigating security alerts in a security operations, incident response or similar role.

• Experience using security tools such as a SIEM, endpoint detection and response platform, or email security platform to investigate suspicious activity.

• An understanding of common threats, such as phishing, account compromise and suspicious endpoint activity, and the networking, operating system and identity concepts needed to investigate them.

• Ability to query and interpret logs, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and recognise when further investigation or escalation is needed.

• Some scripting experience: you can read, adapt and write small scripts in Python or another language to support an investigation or simplify repetitive work.

• Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting findings, explaining uncertainty and providing effective handovers.

• A careful approach to sensitive information, willingness to ask for help, and openness to feedback.

We welcome different routes into security. A particular degree or certification is not required; we’re interested in what you can do, how you approach problems, and what you’re ready to learn next.

An ideal candidate also has:

• Experience investigating activity in cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP, SaaS applications, or identity systems.

• Exposure to writing or tuning detections, threat hunting, or investigating activity across multiple data sources.

• Experience using Python, APIs or automation platforms to improve a security workflow.

• Familiarity with evidence collection or forensic analysis on macOS, Windows or Linux.

You do not need experience in every area above. Bring a solid operational foundation, curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Dev Agents builds in-house and integrates vendors such as Claude and Codex. That includes an Agent Gateway that serves internal MCPs, managed access to skills, and cloud runners that fan work out to cloud agents.

Real-world impact at scale

• Choose which experiments to run for a root cause analysis agent when no playbook exists.

• Decide when to build, integrate or buy as model prices and capabilities shift roughly every quarter.

Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.

As a Firmware Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.

We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.

• Be the first person to make a new board do anything at all. Bring up new platforms and prototypes from virgin silicon: configure I/O, get SPI, I2C, UART, BLE talking, debug system init, validate the design, and turn unproven hardware into a product.

• Build the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.

• Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.

• Solid bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.

• Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.

• Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.

• Cross-team scope. You have contributed to work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have worked effectively across teams to build consensus.

• Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you factor that into your design decisions.

Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, Linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.

As a Firmware Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.

We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

• You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
